title: Flight Centre investigating third-party breach that may have exposed customer records
text:
A third-party accommodation booking system breach may have exposed customer records, including a very small number containing passport details, for Flight Centre and its leisure brands.

Flight Centre Travel Group disclosed on 26 November 2026 that it is investigating a cyber incident involving a third-party accommodation booking system. The company detected unusual activity in a platform used by its leisure travel brands, including Flight Centre, Travel Associates, and Cruiseabout, as well as some independent agents. Flight bookings and corporate travel bookings, which rely on separate systems, were not affected.

According to Reuters, the company has not yet determined the volume of records accessed. Initial reviews indicate that most accessed records contained customer names, while some included basic travel details. Flight Centre believes a very small number of records contained passport details, email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth. In rare cases, records may have included health or mobility information. The company stated it found no evidence that credit card, payment, or bank account details were accessed.

Flight Centre has activated its incident response plan and is investigating with the supplier and cybersecurity firm Mandiant. The company is working to identify affected systems, contain the incident, change authentication keys and passwords, and increase monitoring. It is also notifying relevant authorities and working with external security experts.

title: Cacti zero-day allows unauthenticated remote code execution
text:
A stored SQL injection flaw in Cacti enables attackers to execute commands without login if guest access is enabled, with no patch currently available.

Security researcher ek0ms savi0r disclosed a zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, on 26 November 2026. The flaw, tracked as 4HTTP2ROOT or 4HTTP2SHELL, is a stored SQL injection that allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution in four HTTP requests if anonymous guest access is enabled. A public proof of concept demonstrated command execution on Cacti 1.2.31, though no exploitation in the wild had been reported as of 27 November 2026.

The vulnerability arises because Cacti does not properly validate settings controlled by guests, allowing database changes that affect polling configurations. While the researcher demonstrated root-level command execution on a test system running as root, commands generally run with the permissions of the affected process. Even without root access, a compromised server could expose credentials used to reach network devices, providing a potential route into other systems.

No CVE identifier, official severity rating, or confirmed patch is available at this time. Administrators are advised to remove the designated Guest User from authentication settings and deactivate the guest account under Console > Configuration > Users. While disabling guest access blocks the demonstrated attack path, it does not repair the underlying SQL injection, so t

title: SAP confirms incident after GitHub tokens allegedly stolen
text:
SAP is investigating a security incident where attackers allegedly used stolen employee tokens to alter source code on GitHub, though no customer data breach has been confirmed.

SAP has confirmed an IT security incident following the detection of suspicious activity within its development infrastructure. According to reports from Der Spiegel, which cited an internal memo, the incident is being handled under the name “Project Granite.” The German software maker stated that it detected the activity and took immediate steps to secure its services, while noting that investigators have found no evidence of unauthorised access to customer business data at this stage.

Der Spiegel reported that attackers obtained authentication tokens belonging to SAP employees, enabling them to copy and alter source code stored on GitHub. The publication cited sources suggesting the attack may have involved AI agents, a detail SAP has not confirmed. It remains unclear whether the compromised code was proprietary or part of public repositories, and whether any altered code reached software delivered to customers.

In response to the incident, Handelsblatt reported that SAP has reportedly replaced signing keys, limited access to GitHub, and suspended automated development operations. These emergency measures have reportedly affected numerous teams. SAP has not publicly disclosed which specific repositories were reviewed or whether users need to take action, leaving the scope of the compromise undefi

title: VulnCheck data shows credential harvesting becoming core exploitation trend
text:
Requests to steal credentials rose from 1% to between 25% and 35% of vulnerability exploitation in 2026.

VulnCheck’s canary network data indicates that credential harvesting has shifted from a fringe activity to a major exploitation trend. Between January and November 2026, requests to steal credentials comprised 13% of all recorded vulnerability exploitation, with the monthly share climbing from approximately 1% in January to between 25% and 35% in September and October. The company tracked 694 exploited CVEs during this period, of which attackers used 127 (18%) at least once to target database passwords, cloud keys, API tokens, or SSH keys.

Application secrets were the primary target, with Laravel secrets drawing requests from 4,784 distinct IP addresses and .env files from 2,840. Cloud credentials followed, with AWS keys sought by 1,687 IPs and Google Cloud credentials by 1,007. The vulnerabilities exploited are predominantly recent, with 57% carrying 2025 or 2026 IDs, and are concentrated in open source software, AI products, and developer tools, which account for 77 of the 127 CVEs. Network edge devices accounted for only 10 of the flaws.

The median CVSS score for these vulnerabilities is 9.4, but medium-severity bugs made up only 6% of the list and produced 23% of all harvesting records. This is because file-read and SSRF flaws allow attackers to read secrets without executing code. Notable examples include CVE-2025-30208, a file-read flaw in the Vite frontend tool,

title: Hackers Abuse Microsoft and Mozilla Trusted Signing to Deploy Malware That Steals Browser Passwords
text:
A Windows installer leverages trusted code signing to deploy a browser stealer targeting Brazilian users, with code pointing to a more serious goal of giving remote control of a hidden browser.

Analysts at Rogue Authority identified a Windows installer, HardwareInfo.msi, that delivers browser-stealing malware using signed Windows components and a signed Firefox add-on to look less suspicious. The malware uses DLL side-loading to execute malicious code within a genuine Windows BitLocker helper, renamed ChromeUpdate.exe, to evade detection. It targets saved passwords, session cookies, and autofill records across Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Opera GX, Vivaldi, and Firefox.

The toolkit is tailored for Brazilian users, evidenced by Portuguese settings and references to the country’s electronic invoicing system. On Chromium-based browsers, it installs a fake PDF viewer extension, 'Documentos Online', while Firefox users receive a signed add-on named 'pulsardrift'. The code goes further, preparing a hidden Chrome session that an operator could control on the victim’s own computer, although analysts did not observe that session being used.

Rogue Authority reported the two three-day certificates issued to Technoservice B.V. to Microsoft. The report notes that while the signatures verify the signer and file integrity, they do not guarantee safety. The installer runs without administrator privileges and hides from the installed apps list, using scheduled tasks and startup files for pe

title: Unit 42 tracks AI agents accelerating corporate intrusions
text:
Researchers identified autonomous AI agents used to expand access in over 10 campaigns, reducing command intervals from 23.9 seconds to 1.4 seconds.

Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 published a research report on 24 November 2026 stating that attackers used autonomous AI agents to steal credentials and probe cloud systems in more than 10 campaigns tracked between July and September 2026. The activity targeted government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture, and education organisations.

The most successful intrusions combined human direction with autonomous execution, where a person provided initial access while the agent mapped systems and attempted to expand privileges. In one case, an agent ran approximately 800 unique commands over 140 minutes, surveying websites, databases, and cloud environments. Unit 42 noted that the median gap between commands fell from 23.9 seconds during manual activity to 1.4 seconds after an AI agent took over.

Researchers recovered hundreds of unique script payloads, including PHP web shells and Python credential harvesters, but found no compiled backdoor or single shared malware family. In one instance, an agent used stolen file-sharing credentials to move from a Linux server to a Windows server running Internet Information Services (IIS), where web shells were found in more than 40 locations.

title: Exposed attacker servers reveal US hospital credentials and cloud listing
text:
Analysts at Hunt.io identified exposed web directories containing US hospital credential records, a manufacturer's Azure storage listing, and law firm target maps, highlighting the risks of exposed attacker infrastructure.

Hunt.io analysts published findings on 25 November 2026 regarding three exposed web directories that revealed an intrusion crew's operations. The recovered files included 8,460 unique email addresses and 3,570 authentication records linked to a US hospital system, though researchers could not establish how the records were obtained or if they remained valid. The investigation also uncovered a valid Azure shared access signature (SAS) token used to list 155,568 objects in a manufacturer's cloud storage, exposing data organisation without evidence of file downloads.

In the legal sector, the crew maintained a target list of 563 entries and scanned over 60 named law firms for live VPNs and Citrix gateways. At Simpson Thacher & Bartlett, logs showed the crew tested approximately 100 staff email and password pairs against two Citrix gateways, but the credentials were rejected and no VPN session was recorded. Hunt.io stated that the evidence does not establish a breach of any law firm or federal agency, nor a ransomware link.

The investigation identified malicious software including a Java database driver posing as a legitimate component, an Apollo-derived Windows payload, and a Poseidon-derived Linux implant associated with the Mythic command-and-control frame

title: Drupal installer gap exploited after incomplete patch
text:
Attackers are exploiting a residual flaw in Drupal's installer that was missed by last week's security update, allowing site takeover on systems in unusual states.

Drupal has disclosed CVE-2026-136716, an access bypass vulnerability that enables site takeover, following the release of a patch for CVE-2026-132165 on 18 November. The new issue, disclosed on 25 November, affects sites in 'unusual or incomplete install states' that remained vulnerable after the initial fix. Drupal stated that the flaw is being exploited in the wild and that it is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected state.

The original vulnerability, CVE-2026-132165, was an installer flaw credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner and was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on 24 November. Drupal warned that any site that left its installer remotely accessible following the previous advisory may still have been compromised, even if it is no longer in the vulnerable state.

Patches for the new issue are included in Drupal versions 11.4.14, 11.3.23, and 10.6.23. Affected production sites must run an update hook after upgrading to fully address the vulnerability. Drupal has not identified the responsible party for the exploitation and advised users to check logs for signs of compromise.

title: Standard Chartered's Zodia Custody reports data breach
text:
Zodia Custody confirmed a security incident exposing client and employee contact details, though it reported no unauthorised cryptocurrency transactions.

Standard Chartered’s cryptocurrency custody unit, Zodia Custody, detected attempts to probe its platform on 23 November 2026. Chief Executive Richard Clark told Reuters that the company temporarily suspended its business-to-business API as a precaution before restoring the service after adding security measures. Zodia stated that the API was not identified as the attacker’s entry point.

By 24 November, the company determined that an unauthorised party had accessed publicly available details about client organisations. The exposed records included business contact names and email addresses for a small number of clients and employees. Zodia has contacted affected clients and notified regulators but has not disclosed the exact number of records compromised or how the attacker gained access.

The incident is distinct from confirmed cryptocurrency theft, as the disclosed information did not include private keys used to authorise transfers. Standard Chartered announced definitive acquisition agreements on 21 October and increased its stake in Zodia Custody to 100%. Neither the company nor Reuters linked the intrusion to the acquisition or integration process.

title: Bithumb confirms 15-day breach of internal collaboration system
text:
South Korean exchange Bithumb disclosed that attackers accessed its DaouOffice system for 15 days, stealing passport numbers, bank details, and wallet addresses, raising significant phishing risks.

Bithumb said in a 25 November update that its investigation revealed unauthorised access to its DaouOffice collaboration system from 12 to 27 October, extending far beyond the initially reported one-hour window. The company stated that the breach exposed personal information and files, including copies of identity documents, South Korean resident registration numbers, driver’s license numbers, transaction histories, and contact details.

The affected individuals include customers, employees of partner companies, and current and former staff. Bithumb said the stolen data varied by person and that the initial disclosure covered about 7,100 customers and employees, though it did not provide a new total in the updated notice. The exchange noted that DaouOffice is separate from its trading systems and that it found no evidence of a direct breach of the exchange or its customer database.

Bithumb said it blocked the IP addresses tied to the intrusion, suspended DaouOffice, and worked with the software developer to investigate. The company stated it fixed the security flaw and is reviewing its internet-facing services. It is notifying affected customers by email and text and will tell each person which records were stolen.

title: MalwareMustDie documents early LoongArch Linux RAT in EasyShell family
text:
Researchers identified a Rust-based implant targeting LoongArch Linux, one of the earliest publicly documented remote access trojans for the architecture, highlighting new risks for non-x86 systems.

MalwareMustDie has published an analysis of Linux/EasyShell, a Rust beacon implant delivered via a shell script stager. The malware is hosted on a server in the United States and provides seven builds, including l128 for LoongArch, which the researchers note is one of the earliest publicly documented LoongArch64 RAT implementations found in public reporting as of 21 November 2026. The implant uses the EasyShell framework, a Chinese red team C2 tool, and communicates over HTTPS to a specific API endpoint.

The l32 build, described as a Rust-based HTTPS beacon, includes capabilities for remote shell access, file transfer, and SOCKS5 tunneling. It evades detection by renaming itself to mimic kernel threads, such as [kworker/0:0], and checks for sandbox environments. The report cautions that the LoongArch build is a framework default offered by every EasyShell stager, meaning its presence does not necessarily indicate a targeted campaign against LoongArch hardware. Additionally, the researchers note the build may not function on stock Debian loong64 or Kylin hosts without specific loaders.

For defenders, the report advises against immediately terminating the fake kernel thread, as this destroys live configuration and session keys. Instead, teams should isolate the system, preserve p

title: PolinRider malware hidden in GitHub pull requests for three open-source projects
text:
Attackers inserted password-stealing malware into build workflows for AsyncAPI, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts, with malicious installers published for download.

Researchers at StepSecurity identified PolinRider malware in open-source projects AsyncAPI Generator, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts. The attackers used force-pushes to insert malicious JavaScript loaders into pull requests from the GitHub account Eternity0207, which was later suspended. The code was disguised as fonts or hidden in build files, with some changes remaining visible for only 30 to 40 minutes before being replaced.

At CircuitVerse, the malicious code ran in the automated release workflow, resulting in the publication of 40 infected installers for Windows, Linux and macOS. Maintainers removed these files on 25 November 2026, more than a month after they became available. Open Food Facts ran builds on four affected commits, all of which failed, and maintainers rotated a secret. AsyncAPI required approval for external workflows, so its affected pull requests did not run in continuous integration.

Victims who examined infected machines reported that later stages targeted browser passwords, macOS Keychain data and GitHub credentials. StepSecurity found the loader in 576 of 622 repositories it checked across 311 GitHub accounts. The malware used Ethereum data to locate its next-stage server, meaning blocking a single IP address would not cover the campaign.

title: North Korea-linked PolinRider poisons 7,600 GitHub repos
text:
SafeDep reports that threat actors linked to North Korea have compromised over 7,600 GitHub repositories to distribute malware via a Python loader.

SafeDep has identified a campaign dubbed PolinRider, in which threat actors linked to North Korea have planted a Python loader in GitHub repositories. The firm stated that evidence suggests the activity may have begun as far back as February 2025.

According to SafeDep, the loader is concealed within a small utils package or in conftest.py files. When Python imports the file, the loader reads the newest transaction. The report indicates that more than 7,600 repositories have been affected by this supply chain poisoning.

title: Google mandates MCP or CLI for Workspace AI agents from February 2027
text:
Google is restricting how autonomous AI agents access Workspace data, requiring them to use new Model Context Protocol servers or a command-line interface to enforce security controls.

Google has announced that, from 1 February 2027, AI agents must connect to Google Workspace via its new Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or the Workspace command-line interface (CLI). The company stated that traditional REST APIs, designed for human-paced applications, are insufficient for autonomous agents operating at machine speed, necessitating built-in security checks and data access restrictions.

The MCP servers support Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat, and Tasks, with Google Keep support planned. These interfaces enforce organisational permissions, data loss prevention (DLP) policies, and classification labels. Additionally, the servers require human confirmation for sensitive operations, such as sending emails or modifying sharing permissions, and reject non-agent OAuth clients.

For Google Cloud, agents will receive individual identities through the Agent Registry, governed by identity and access management (IAM) policies. The new Google Cloud Agent Gateway will verify agent identities, enforce default-deny outbound rules, and use the Model Armor service to screen requests for prompt injection. The Workspace AI Tools Addendum also prohibits the permanent storage of raw Workspace data for model training and sets a 30-day retention limit for certain technic

title: Kaspersky detects Keenadu malware on over 220,000 Android devices
text:
Preinstalled malware in Android firmware has surged 2.5-fold in a year, with Keenadu and Triada affecting 88% of infected devices, posing persistent risks to corporate fleets.

Kaspersky reports that the number of Android devices detected with preinstalled malware has increased by more than 2.5 times over the past year. In the first ten months of 2026, the Keenadu family was found on more than 220,000 devices. Together with the older Triada family, these two malware families account for 88% of devices identified with preinstalled malware this year.

The malware is introduced via supply chain attacks, where manufacturers or contractors install malicious firmware. Once embedded in the system partition, Kaspersky states it is technically impossible for antivirus tools or the operating system to remove it, and some variants persist even after reflashing. The latest Triada versions feature a modular architecture allowing attackers to inject malicious functionality into any app and tailor payloads to specific targets.

Keenadu backdoors typically remain dormant for approximately two and a half months before activation via command-and-control servers, a delay intended to evade detection. In most known cases, the malware is used for ad fraud, specifically generating fake clicks. For enterprises, infected devices can lead to performance degradation, account hijacking, data leakage, and enlistment in DDoS botnets.

title: FIFA confirms cyberattack exposed limited personal and business data
text:
FIFA has confirmed that hackers accessed internal systems, following a claim by the Handsome Boy Hacking Club that it stole over 12 GB of data.

The Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) stated on 26 November that it was the victim of a cyberattack resulting in the "unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information." The organisation said it is working closely with relevant authorities, including law enforcement, and condemned the "unlawful acquisition and publication" of the data.

The Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) claimed last week that it stole more than 12 GB of data from FIFA and attempted to extort the organisation. The group said it accessed FIFA’s Microsoft environment and published the stolen data on a cybercriminal forum. The data allegedly includes identity and immigration documents, financial records, legal documents, and governance information.

FIFA did not respond to follow-up questions regarding the specific nature of the incident. The breach follows recent cyberattacks on other European soccer entities, including LaLiga and the French Football Federation.

title: CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers
text:
CISA has issued an advisory for a critical, unpatched buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, which have recently been targeted in attacks across European supermarkets.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued an ICS advisory on 24 November regarding CVE-2026-129713, a stack-based buffer overflow in the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controllers. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and allows remote attackers to send specially crafted HTTP/S POST requests without authentication, leading to memory corruption, web server restart, and potential arbitrary code execution with web server privileges.

Danfoss confirmed on 20 November that the flaw will be addressed in upcoming software version 5.5.x, but no patch is currently available. The update will also remove the option for customers to disable 'Strict mode'. CISA notes that the controllers are deployed worldwide, though the exact number remains unclear.

This advisory follows two waves of attacks in recent weeks linked to Iranian state actors. Between 11 and 12 October, French supermarkets suffered losses after attacks attributed to Iran’s IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit compromised Danfoss and Copeland/Dixell controllers to alter defrost settings. A second wave on 1 and 2 November affected at least 115 stores across Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, Romania, and Estonia, with supplier Sabcobel stating the attackers used the same vulnerability seen in the earlier

title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in $43.9bn all-stock deal
text:
The record-breaking acquisition combines endpoint security with zero-trust network access, aiming to create a single control plane to deploy and control AI.

CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion, making it the largest cybersecurity acquisition to date. The deal surpasses Google’s $32 billion purchase of Wiz and is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal 2028. Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, valuing Zscaler at $260.41 per share based on recent closing prices.

The merger combines CrowdStrike’s endpoint security with Zscaler’s cloud-delivered zero-trust access, creating a single platform with a common data layer. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz stated the move is designed to address the shift from connecting people to places to connecting AI agents to data. The companies plan to integrate Falcon and Zscaler’s Zero Trust Exchange to provide unified policy enforcement. Kurtz described the planned integration with an example of an agent on a laptop pulling sensitive information and sending it to an unapproved AI model, noting that together it would be one detection, one decision, and one kill switch that stops the agent on the device and cuts its path on the network.

CrowdStrike expects the combined entity to generate more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue at closing, with an additional $1 billion in annualised revenue projected wi

title: Signal blocks OS AI agents from reading chats
text:
Signal has implemented platform-specific measures to prevent iOS and Android AI agents from accessing user messages, citing a lack of control over data collection by operating system features.

Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation, described AI agents integrated into operating systems, such as Google Gemini on Android and Apple's Siri AI, as "an existential threat to Signal" in a 20 November blog post. The organisation stated it could not control what these agents collected, prompting the deployment of new protections to stop them from capturing user chats.

On Android, Signal said the existing 'Screen security' setting would switch on automatically when an AI assistant attempts to read the screen. The company explained that because multiple Android versions exist, there is no reliable way to detect screenshot attempts if screenshots are already disabled, so it chose detection over blocking all screenshots to preserve user experience. On iOS 27, Signal is preventing screenshots and displaying a 'Block Siri AI' setting. However, on macOS 27, Signal said it had no dependable way to stop screenshots, as Apple's screen-protection options cover only streaming and copy-protected media.

Signal also noted that third-party agents, such as Meta Muse, use accessibility settings to reach app data. The company has asked Apple, Google, and Microsoft for a documented way for apps to opt out of AI access to screens, files, and notifications without breaking functionality.

title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services in 11-country operation
text:
Law enforcement from 11 countries disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services, identifying 321 websites and tracing over €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions.

Authorities from 11 countries, supported by Europol, the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), INTERPOL, and the European Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance (AAPA), have disrupted 57 illegal streaming services. According to a Europol press release, the operation identified 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content, which collectively recorded over 7.3 million visits annually.

Investigators traced more than €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions, with further analysis ongoing. To achieve this, they partnered with crypto industry experts from Binance, Coinbase, and Chainalysis to link illegal IPTV services, crypto wallets, and the individuals controlling them. The operation targeted a market where providers sell unauthorised access to premium television channels, live sports, and films, often collecting payments via cryptocurrency to obscure the origin of profits.

The European Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance (AAPA) stated that legitimate service providers lose around €4.83 billion annually as roughly 60 million people in Europe use illegal platforms. This action follows several recent operations, including Operation KRATOS 2 in June, which removed over 27,000 illegal streaming URLs and led to 29 arrests, and Operation Switch Off in January, which seized three industrial-scale illegal IPTV servi

title: ShinyHunters claims return via new Tor site after member arrests
text:
The extortion group has relaunched its data leak site, using historical PGP keys to assert legitimacy following a series of international arrests targeting its members.

ShinyHunters has announced its return on a new Tor-based data leak site launched on 23 November 2026, following a period of inactivity after law enforcement operations targeted alleged members. The group’s statement, published in Russian and English, distances itself from former members and denounces those who have been arrested and are reportedly cooperating with authorities. The operators claim to be the original group, stating that "a lot has happened recently" and noting that their main representative had stopped responding and their Telegram account was deleted.

To verify their identity, the new operators signed verification messages using two historical ShinyHunters PGP keys dating back to 2020. BleepingComputer confirmed that the signatures match known public keys associated with the group, including one used to authenticate communications in August 2025. However, these keys were revoked in March 2026, and the group stated at that time that the older keys would no longer be used. The new announcement also introduces a new PGP key, but notably, none of the messages were signed with the March 2026 replacement key, leaving it unclear if the new operators possess that specific private key.

The group’s return follows the arrest of several individuals linked to ShinyHunters, including a 24-year-old Amsterd

title: Unclassified CIA system breached in cyberattack, AP source says
text:
A person familiar with the incident told the Associated Press that an unclassified CIA system handling open-source intelligence was compromised, though no classified data was accessed.

An unclassified system at the US Central Intelligence Agency was breached in a cyberattack, according to a person familiar with the incident who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity. The source stated that the breach did not involve any classified information and that the issue has been resolved.

The affected system handles open-source intelligence, which involves the collection and analysis of publicly available data from sources including the internet, commercial satellites and private data brokers. While this information is generally public or semi-public, it can provide intelligence analysts with significant insight when combined with data from classified programmes.

It remains unclear what specific information was compromised or who was responsible for the attack. The incident was first reported by The New York Times on Tuesday and comes amid a series of other high-profile system failures and outages affecting US critical infrastructure and major technology firms.

title: Attackers use stolen AI prompt credentials to probe AWS infrastructure
text:
Security firm Dragos traced AWS API calls to credentials planted in AI prompts, revealing that attackers are harvesting secrets from AI hosting providers.

Dragos reported that between July and November 2026, it sent nearly two million prompts containing unique links and decoy AWS access keys to AI hosting providers. The firm found evidence that attackers obtained approximately 200 of these test keys, some of which were tested within hours of submission. The stolen credentials generated tens of thousands of AWS API calls, indicating active exploitation of the exposed data.

Analysis of the activity shows that after validating the keys, the attackers listed Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) buckets and searched AWS Secrets Manager and Systems Manager Parameter Store. Dragos also recorded attempts to enable hosted models in Amazon Bedrock and create new AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users, actions that could provide persistent access even if the original keys are revoked. The firm noted that some affected requests were rejected before the model ran, suggesting the theft occurred at the point where the provider first received traffic.

Malwarebytes noted that attackers obtained credentials even from prompts that hosting providers rejected. Neither Malwarebytes nor Dragos identified a specific malware family behind the theft. The activity did not rely on an AWS software flaw; instead, it leveraged valid credentials presented by the attackers. Dragos emphasised that en

title: NCSC issues guidance to counter agentic offensive frameworks
text:
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre has published an eight-point plan to help defenders mitigate the surge in automated attacks from agentic offensive frameworks.

The NCSC published new guidance on 24 November 2026 to address the growing threat of autonomous offensive frameworks (AOFs) such as ARTEX, Cairn, PentAGI, RedAmon, Xalgorix, and Darkmoon. While these tools originated as legitimate penetration testing utilities, the agency noted they are now being used by threat actors to execute low-cost, automated attacks at scale.

According to the NCSC, these frameworks do not typically exploit novel or known vulnerabilities. Instead, they target 'low-hanging fruit' such as API weaknesses, default or leaked credentials, and misconfigurations in infrastructure as code. Cybersecurity intelligence firm Infrawatch has tracked 10,848 services across 8,105 hosts running these AOFs, highlighting the breadth of the exposure.

The agency's eight-point plan focuses on foundational hygiene rather than advanced AI defence, which it acknowledges will take time to mature. Key recommendations include rigorous asset management to identify externally accessible infrastructure, locking down perimeter services, and ensuring error messages do not leak information that agents can use to plan subsequent moves.

Further measures include deploying bot challenges, applying rate limits at the API level, and throttling account creation from disposable email services. The NCSC also advises placing hone

title: Drupal RCE flaw CVE-2026-132165 actively exploited
text:
CISA has added a critical Drupal vulnerability to its KEV Catalog after confirming active exploitation that allows site takeover via the installer.

The Drupal security team confirmed that CVE-2026-132165, a critical remote code execution flaw, has been actively exploited on live sites since at least 19 November 2026. Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, the vulnerability allows anonymous users to abuse the Drupal installer to reinstall the core, leading to site takeover or remote code execution.

CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday, ordering federal agencies to remediate by Friday, 27 November 2026. The agency noted that such vulnerabilities pose significant risks to the federal enterprise and encouraged all organisations to prioritise remediation of KEV Catalog entries.

While the paid Drupal Steward Web Application Firewall service mitigates known attack vectors, the security team advised upgrading to the latest available version. If immediate patching is not possible, administrators should block access to /core/install.php via web server configuration or .htaccess files.

title: Turnitin investigating unauthorised activity on customer-facing systems
text:
Education technology firm Turnitin has disclosed unauthorised activity on certain customer-facing systems, with the University of Colorado Boulder monitoring its integration.

Turnitin, a subsidiary of Advance Publications, confirmed on 23 November that it identified unauthorised activity involving certain customer-facing systems. CEO Chris Caren stated in a letter on the company’s website that the incident response plan was immediately initiated, relevant authorities were notified, and an investigation was launched with external cyber experts.

The company said its systems are fully operational and safe to use, and that these customer-facing systems do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information. However, Turnitin did not specify which systems might have been affected or whether any data was accessed. Customer-facing systems include the student submission portal, instructor grading interface, integration APIs, and reporting dashboards.

The University of Colorado Boulder said it was in contact with Turnitin to determine if any of its information was compromised. The university’s Office of Information Technology stated it had no indication that student or instructor information, assignments, or other data were exposed, and added additional monitoring to its Canvas integration to ensure it had not been impacted.

title: NCC Group: Ransomware claims rise 23% in October
text:
A new report indicates a sharp increase in claimed ransomware incidents, driven by AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the emergence of new extortion brands.

NCC Group has reported that claimed ransomware attacks surged by 23% in October 2026, reaching 1,049 incidents. This follows a record-breaking third quarter for 2026. The researchers attribute the spike to the growing use of artificial intelligence to rapidly identify vulnerabilities and chained attack paths, describing it as an early indicator of a new cyber environment where serious flaws are weaponised more quickly.

The Gentlemen ransomware group claimed the highest number of victims in October with 139 incidents, followed closely by N0n, a new actor first observed in September 2026, which claimed 133 victims. N0n has also claimed responsibility for data breaches affecting JPMorgan, Mastercard, and Visa. Qilin placed third with 131 claimed attacks. NCC Group noted that several newer groups established in 2026, including Booba Project, Emperador, and Wallstreet, made up the rest of the top 10, though their origins remain unknown and they have not been conclusively linked to specific countries or predecessors.

The industrials sector was the most heavily targeted, accounting for 31% of claimed attacks, followed by consumer discretionary (19%), healthcare (12%), and IT (10%). North America was the most targeted region, representing 46% of attacks, with Europe following at 23%.

title: Fake WordPress plugin bypasses 2FA and serves malicious scripts
text:
Wordfence identified a hidden plugin that creates valid login sessions without 2FA and relays attacker-controlled JavaScript to visitors.

Researchers from the Wordfence Threat Intelligence Team identified a fake WordPress plugin during incident response investigations in January and September 2026. The malware hides from the WordPress dashboard and uses generated names, stylesheets, and configuration files to appear legitimate. Approximately two-thirds of the plugin files consist of filler, with the active malware contained in PHP and JavaScript components.

The plugin contains a backdoor that creates a valid WordPress login session for an existing account, bypassing standard password and two-factor authentication checks. Changing an administrator’s password does not invalidate this access while the malicious code remains active. Additionally, the plugin manipulates file timestamps to match existing plugins, making detection via recently modified files difficult.

For non-logged-in visitors, the plugin relays JavaScript from an attacker-controlled server through the infected site. This obfuscates the traffic source, making it appear as if the script originated from the legitimate website. Wordfence stated the loader could support phishing forms, fake update prompts, malicious redirects, or keystroke logging, though these are potential uses rather than confirmed outcomes in the observed incidents.

title: New gang Inception denies ShinyHunters rebranding claims
text:
Security researchers have theorised that the data theft and extortion group Inception is a rebrand of ShinyHunters, a claim the new crew has explicitly rejected.

A new data theft and extortion gang known as Inception has emerged, leading security researchers to theorise that it is a rebrand of the previously active ShinyHunters group. The attribution is based on the group's operational similarities, with researchers noting that Inception "looks and acts just like ShinyHunters".

In response to these theories, Inception has issued a statement rejecting the attribution. The group claims it has no affiliation with ShinyHunters, asserting that it is a distinct entity despite the perceived operational parallels.

The dispute highlights the difficulty in tracking threat actor rebranding, where groups may change names to evade detection while maintaining similar tactics, techniques, and procedures.

title: US Treasury's FinCEN takes systems offline after cyber incident
text:
The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network has disconnected some systems to investigate unauthorised access, causing temporary service disruptions and filing deadline extensions.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), the US Treasury Department’s financial intelligence unit, has disconnected some of its systems while investigating a cyber incident. In a notice on the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) E-Filing System website, the agency stated it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorised access to a limited subset of its systems.

As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline. The website remains operational, but some FinCEN services may be temporarily unavailable. The agency has extended deadlines for qualifying filers affected by the disruption, granting temporary, limited exception relief in response to the service hindering reporting obligations.

FinCEN has not shared further details on the nature of the incident or made any mention of a potential data breach. It is currently unclear who was behind the attack or if any data was accessed or stolen. The agency said it is working to return all systems to normal.

title: Ransomware hits Port of Santos and Argentinian pipeline
text:
Industrial sectors in Latin America face a surge in ransomware, with recent attacks affecting major infrastructure in Brazil and Argentina.

On 6 November, a ransomware attack encrypted data at the Port of Santos in Brazil, the largest port in South America. A simultaneous power outage at the port's data centre is under investigation, though the Santos Port Authority (APS) stated that operations were not disrupted, mainly because the authority switched to alternate processes. APS restored its enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and customer services on 24 November, noting that the intruder likely gained entry via a malicious email or infected website.

The incident is part of a broader trend in the region. Dragos reported that industrial organisations in South America suffered at least 82 claimed ransomware incidents in the third quarter of 2026, up from 64 in the previous quarter. Brazil recorded 22 incidents, while Peru and Argentina each tallied 16. Abdul Alamri, a principal threat intelligence analyst at Dragos, noted that while operational technology (OT) systems were not directly compromised in these cases, disruptions to enterprise IT and ERP systems often cascade into operational stoppages.

In Argentina, pipeline company Oldelval reported a cybersecurity incident affecting administrative systems, according to filings with the National Securities Commission. The company stated that the movement of oil and crude was not hampered. However, Alamri cautioned that s

title: Aikido finds 42 phishing pages on Hugging Face
text:
Attackers used Hugging Face's DeepSite AI to create fake login pages for 28 brands, including Microsoft and Google, to harvest credentials.

Aikido Security identified 42 pages on Hugging Face Spaces that impersonated 28 brands, including Microsoft, Google, PayPal, Chase, and Coinbase. Researchers linked 29 of these pages to DeepSite, an AI website builder, through project tags and change records. The pages were hosted at hf.space addresses, using HTTPS encryption that did not verify brand ownership.

Aikido discovered the pages on 16 October 2026 and reported them to Hugging Face the same day. At that time, 34 pages were live and eight were paused. By 29 October 2026, all 42 pages were paused or no longer publicly reachable. Researchers noted that one fake Microsoft login page had 15 recorded changes, 14 of which occurred within approximately 90 minutes, suggesting automated generation rather than manual coding.

Some pages requested one-time sign-in codes, card details, or personal information in addition to passwords. One Microsoft clone redirected visitors to the real Outlook site after collecting their information. Researchers could not determine how many users interacted with the pages or entered credentials, as visitor records were unavailable.

title: ShinyHunters alleged return claimed as Inception denies ties
text:
A new extortion group called Inception has emerged, while someone claiming to represent ShinyHunters has announced the group’s alleged return, prompting denial from Inception operators.

An account linked to ShinyHunters since 2020 posted a message on the Exploit forum announcing the group’s alleged return, providing a new leak site address and PGP key. The authors disavowed other hackers claiming membership and stated they would not be active on other forums. However, DataBreaches noted that the original PGP key had reportedly been leaked, meaning the identity of the posters cannot be fully verified and impostors may be capitalising on the name.

Separately, a new cybercrime group named Inception has emerged, with its leak site listing major US companies including AMD, PepsiCo, Lucid Motors, Henry Schein, and Cigna Healthcare. Okta research suggests Inception may involve hackers previously associated with ShinyHunters, tracked as O-UNC-053, noting that phishing activity dropped during arrests in September and October before resuming in November. Inception has denied any connection to ShinyHunters, stating that shared use of commodity services and overlapping targets do not constitute operational linkage.

ReversingLabs identified 21 confirmed phishing domains associated with Inception, suggesting potential targeting of companies such as Anthropic, Amazon, Adobe, Nintendo, Netflix, OpenAI, and Tesla. There is no indication that these specific entities were successfully compro

title: Adobe patches critical flaws in Experience Manager and Campaign Classic
text:
Adobe released updates on 24 November 2026 to fix critical vulnerabilities in Experience Manager and Campaign Classic that allow code execution and privilege escalation.

Adobe published security bulletins APSB26-104 and APSB26-194 on 24 November 2026, addressing critical vulnerabilities in Adobe Experience Manager and Adobe Campaign Classic. The updates fix flaws with CVSS 3.1 scores of up to 9.9, including code injection and SQL injection issues that could allow attackers to execute malicious code or gain unauthorized access. Adobe stated it was not aware of any attacks using these flaws at the time of publication, and CISA does not list them as known exploited.

For Experience Manager, the critical code injection vulnerabilities CVE-2026-123266 and CVE-2026-132877 allow a low-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code without user interaction. The affected versions include Experience Manager Cloud Service 2026.10.29251 and earlier, Experience Manager 6.5 Service Pack 26 and earlier, and Experience Manager 6.5 LTS Service Pack 3 and earlier. Adobe provides cumulative hotfixes for specific service packs and a fixed cloud release, 2026.11.29643.

The Campaign Classic bulletin covers 12 critical flaws in on-premises deployments on Windows and Linux. These include code injection, SQL injection, and authorisation flaws. Organisations running Campaign Classic 7.4.4 build 9403 or earlier must move to build 9404, while those on 7.4.5 build 9420 or earlier should move to build 94

title: InfraTrust: Exploited supply chain flaws dominate recent advisories
text:
Eclypsium's November report highlights that most critical infrastructure vulnerabilities are in bundled third-party software, creating patching delays for enterprises.

Eclypsium's November InfraTrust Pulse report, covering 373 advisories from 23 vendors between 15 October and 19 November 2026, found that 33 of the 38 advisories addressing vulnerabilities in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogue fixed flaws in bundled components such as PHP, Node.js, and OpenSSH. This supply-chain dependency means organisations must wait for infrastructure vendors to incorporate upstream fixes, extending exposure windows even after the original developer releases a patch.

The report notes that the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) are being exploited in attacks against Palo Alto Networks and Check Point firewalls. Threat actors have chained these PHP flaws with other vulnerabilities to gain root access, with Check Point reporting destructive attacks that deployed data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts. As of 20 November, fixes for PHP2Shell were either partially available or not yet released for affected products from Fortinet, Juniper, Lenovo, HPE, Netgear, HP, and Siemens.

InfraTrust advises administrators to prioritise immediate patching for several actively exploited flaws, including Cisco Expressway (CVE-2026-76466), Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-114625), and SonicWall SonicOS (CVE-2026-19868). The report warns that as AI model

title: Todoist breach exposes user data and integration tokens
text:
An attacker accessed Todoist production systems via stolen credentials, exfiltrating account records for roughly 6% of users and compromising Outlook mailbox data.

Todoist confirmed that an attacker breached its production systems on 23 November 2026, downloading account records for approximately 6% of its user base. The compromised data included email addresses, account creation dates, and older password hashes stored as salted SHA-1, rather than plaintext passwords. The company stated it blocked the attacker’s access and began notifying affected users on 24 November.

According to the incident report, the breach originated from a stolen credential linked to the system managing code changes. The attacker modified automated workflows in three code repositories, obtained additional credentials, and assumed control of an employee’s work account to access the cloud environment. While the attacker could read source code, investigators found no evidence of changes to the application code. Security monitoring flagged an unexpected administrator account at 17:01 UTC on 23 November, hours after the initial data download.

The attacker also retrieved Todoist API and Slack integration tokens for about 0.003% of users and accessed data from connected Outlook mailboxes for roughly 0.001% of users. This included sender details, subject lines, up to 255 characters of message text, and attachment details. Todoist stated it found no bulk download of its task and comment database. The compan

title: Microsoft: Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon using Artex AI tool
text:
Microsoft reported that Chinese state-backed groups are using the Artex AI platform to automate network reconnaissance and exploitation at machine speed.

Microsoft said on Wednesday that Chinese state-backed groups Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon have integrated Artex, an AI-powered platform, into their toolsets. The company stated the groups are using it for "network reconnaissance, credential attacks, and web application exploitation," including searching public repositories for exposed secrets and scanning internet-facing systems.

According to Microsoft, Artex allows threat actors to define specific goals and use AI agents to advance from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access in a matter of minutes. The tool does not introduce new attack techniques but uses common penetration testing tools, often transmitting distinctive characteristics associated with those tools.

Microsoft noted that while Artex does not hide its activity by default, threat actors can vary network indicators like source IP addresses or user agent strings to bypass static detection. The most reliable signal of Artex activity is behavioural: it sends a wide variety of requests in a brief time and retries variations on the same technique at machine speed.

title: Roundcube Webmail patches 12 flaws in 1.6.22 and 1.7.7
text:
Roundcube released updates on 23 November 2026 to fix 12 security vulnerabilities, including issues with attachment handling and unencrypted connections.

Roundcube released versions 1.6.22 and 1.7.7 on 23 November 2026 to address 12 security flaws in its browser-based email client. The updates fix weaknesses in how the software handles attachments, displays messages, and connects to mail servers. The release notes describe flaws that could expose data and allow unauthorised email filter code to run, but they do not confirm remote code execution on the webmail server or report active exploitation of these bugs.

One fix stops Roundcube from passing unsafe PDF, PostScript, and SVG attachment content to ImageMagick, a tool used to process images. The project also revisited an HTTP request injection flaw in its ATD spellcheck backend. Several other fixes address how Roundcube displays HTML email, including two flaws that let message styling break out of limits meant to keep it separate from the webmail interface, and another that let SVG content load external resources despite user remote-content settings.

The update also closes a flaw that could expose responses handled by the CSS proxy and fixes a gap in the HTML filter on systems running PHP versions earlier than 8.4. Two separate flaws could let unauthorised instructions enter Sieve scripts, while another fix addresses XML injection in the XIMSS driver of Roundcube’s password plugin. title: Microsoft warns state-backed groups use ARTEX AI agents for rapid intrusions
text:
Microsoft identified six threat actors, including Storm-0940, using the ARTEX framework to automate credential theft and privileged access in cloud environments.

In a report published on 25 November, Microsoft warned that state-backed and financially motivated groups are abusing ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing framework, to accelerate intrusions. The framework uses AI agents to move from scanning to persistent, privileged access within minutes, reducing the need for manual operator intervention between steps.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence researchers identified six threat actors using ARTEX: Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon, and Salt Typhoon. In one instance, an agent extracted data from Azure Key Vault in five minutes after finding secrets in public GitHub repositories. Microsoft’s investigation into the ConnectWise supply chain campaign found that China-aligned Storm-0940 used ARTEX to accelerate intrusions. In multiple Storm-0940 intrusions, Microsoft observed the group reach privileged cloud access less than three hours after initial targeting, recording over 151,000 failed sign-ins in one campaign.

Defenders should look for sequences of events rather than single indicators, such as bursts of web requests followed by successful access or unusual server processes. title: Iranian group Volant Manticore targets Cypriot organisations
text:
A previously undocumented Iranian threat group is conducting espionage against Cypriot entities to gather intelligence for Tehran.

Dark Reading reports that a new Iranian threat group, designated "Volant Manticore", is actively targeting organisations in Cyprus. The campaign is described as an intelligence-gathering effort conducted on behalf of the Iranian government.

The group was previously undocumented, indicating a new or previously unattributed actor in the threat landscape. The primary objective of the intrusion is espionage, focusing on the collection of sensitive information from Cypriot targets.

No specific vulnerabilities or exploited CVEs were detailed in the source material. The report highlights the geopolitical nature of the threat, linking the activity directly to Iranian state interests.

title: FIFA confirms breach; HBHC claims 12.2 GB data leak
text:
FIFA has confirmed unauthorised access to personal and business data, though it has not verified the Handsome Boy Hacking Club's claim of a 12.2 GB archive.

FIFA confirmed on 25 November that hackers gained unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information. The organisation stated it is working with relevant authorities, including law enforcement, and condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of data. FIFA did not specify how the intrusion occurred, when it was detected, or which systems were affected.

The Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) claims to have obtained and published 12.2 GB of sensitive internal documents, including identity records, executive information, and financial files. Dark Web Informer reported that HBHC stated the files were taken from FIFA’s Microsoft environment and internal governance systems, though the claim remains unverified. The group also claimed it attempted to extort FIFA before posting the files on a cybercrime forum.

Cyber Security News noted that the claimed archive size is a poor measure of the breach’s impact, as large archives may contain duplicate or corrupted data. No public confirmation indicates that FIFA’s files were encrypted. If Microsoft cloud services were involved, audit logs could help investigators check for unusual sign-ins and trace which files were accessed or downloaded.

title: CIA OSINT system reportedly breached; FinCEN takes systems offline
text:
Unknown attackers reportedly used the ARTEX AI framework to breach an unclassified CIA system, while FinCEN disclosed a separate incident prompting precautionary system shutdowns.

According to a source familiar with the matter, unknown attackers reportedly breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). The source told The New York Times that the cyberattack was carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. The CIA and ODNI have not yet replied to requests for details, but the source stated that the hack did not involve classified networks or information, and no other systems are currently at risk.

In a related development, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed it is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. After detecting the attack, the agency took some systems offline as a precaution and instructed banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports. A FinCEN official stated that Treasury is working with the FBI, CISA, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident. While forensic analysis remains ongoing, there is no evidence of any breach of beneficial ownership databases or the Bank Secrecy Act.

title: Switzerland confirms first AI-agent cyberattacks on critical infrastructure
text:
Swiss and Italian agencies report successful intrusions using autonomous AI agents, urging immediate patching of internet-facing systems.

Switzerland’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has confirmed its first reports of cyberattacks against local organisations carried out with the assistance of AI agents. The agency stated that in every known case, the use of these agents led to the successful compromise of the victim’s IT systems, affecting operators in at least two critical infrastructure sectors. The NCSC noted that the number of publicly available AI agents accessible over the internet has nearly doubled since October 2026.

The attacks utilised what the NCSC terms “Agentic Offensive Frameworks,” which can search for vulnerabilities, select attack tools, and adapt tactics with limited human input. CSIRT Italia reported similar large-scale campaigns where multiple AI agents worked in parallel to compromise systems within hours, chaining low-impact vulnerabilities into complex attack chains. The agencies identified ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness - Red Team, and PentAGI as frameworks involved in recent incidents.

The NCSC warns that these tools significantly reduce the time available for defenders to detect and respond to intrusions. It advises organisations to reduce their internet attack surface, restrict access via geo-blocking or IP allow lists, and ensure all internal resources reachable from the internet, such as webmail and VPNs, are protected by multi-

title: 1Password breach exposes customer data via compromised GitHub account
text:
1Password disclosed that an attacker accessed backend systems through a hijacked employee GitHub account, stealing customer names and emails, though vault contents remained secure.

1Password disclosed on 25 November 2026 that an attacker compromised an employee’s corporate GitHub account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services. The intruder downloaded administrative records for a subset of customers, including names, sign-in email addresses, account identifiers, and creation dates. The company stated that customer vault contents, password keys, and account recovery keys were not accessed, and its applications continued to operate normally.

The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and accessed the company’s continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) system, which holds infrastructure credentials. 1Password said the copied code contained no user secrets. The breach also exposed tokens from certain emailed invitations and recovery links; however, the company noted these tokens could not grant access by themselves and required a single sign-on login or a separate code sent to the user’s registered email address.

1Password disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked stolen tokens, and rotated potentially exposed internal credentials. It tightened GitHub and deployment controls and engaged independent cybersecurity experts to validate the cleanup. As a precaution, the company changed invitation and recovery codes from six digits

title: Cisco UCS UEFI Shell flaw allows Secure Boot bypass
text:
Cisco has released fixes for a high-severity vulnerability in UCS servers and appliances that permits attackers to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation.

Cisco has published an advisory for CVE-2026-20293, a vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances. The flaw, rated with a CVSS base score of 7.1, is caused by the availability of memory write commands in the UEFI Shell while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled.

According to Cisco, an authenticated attacker with user or admin credentials, or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access, could exploit this by selecting the UEFI Shell boot option and using shell commands to modify UEFI memory variables. A successful exploit allows the attacker to manipulate the preboot environment, overwrite UEFI Secure Boot-related memory values, and execute unauthorized software.

Cisco has released software updates that address the vulnerability by removing memory modification commands from the shell when Secure Boot is enabled. The vendor states there are no workarounds available and advises customers to upgrade to the fixed software releases listed in the advisory.

title: Ghostscript sandbox escape enables RCE via crafted file uploads
text:
Security firm pwn.ai demonstrated that a now-patched Ghostscript flaw allows crafted file uploads to escape the sandbox and execute remote code on Linux servers.

Security firm pwn.ai has demonstrated a vulnerability in Ghostscript that allows an attacker to escape the program's security sandbox and execute commands on the server. The flaw is triggered by crafted file uploads, specifically PDFs, PostScript files, or images, which are often processed by Ghostscript on Linux servers without the application calling it directly.

The researchers noted that many applications rely on Ghostscript to convert uploaded documents into other formats, creating a significant attack surface for remote code execution. The vulnerability has since been patched by the vendor.

Defenders should ensure their systems are updated with the latest security fixes to mitigate this risk.

title: OpenRouter removes three providers after prompt theft
text:
Researchers at Dragos discovered that attackers stole data from three AI inference providers for months, including requests marked as Zero Data Retention.

Industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos said this week that attackers stole data from inside three AI inference providers for months. The providers did not know about the breach until researchers informed them.

Some of the stolen requests were flagged as Zero Data Retention, a setting intended to ensure that prompts are never stored. OpenRouter, a gateway that routes customers' AI requests to a pool of providers, subsequently dropped the three affected providers.

title: Bulgaria reveals five-year government data breach
text:
Bulgarian authorities discovered a cyberespionage campaign active since 2021 that exfiltrated 130 GB of sensitive state documents, highlighting critical gaps in national security monitoring.

Bulgaria’s Ministry for Innovation and Digital Transformation announced the discovery of a hacking operation that had been running undetected since 2021. According to Reuters, more than 130 GB of documents, equating to approximately 62 million pages, were downloaded from government databases over the five-year period. The stolen files reportedly include cabinet documents, reports, and communications between ministries and government agencies.

The intrusion was only identified in August after the introduction of a new national cybersecurity monitoring system, which flagged suspicious activity. Minister Ivan Vassilev stated that there is currently no evidence that the personal data of Bulgarian citizens was compromised. While several international hacking groups are suspected, investigators have not yet linked the attack to a specific country or nation-state actor.

In response, authorities isolated affected systems, blocked attacker access, and removed malware. Intelligence services, the defence ministry, police, and international partners, including the EU’s cybersecurity agency, joined the response. Prosecutors have been informed to investigate both the external attackers and potential internal failures in detecting the intrusion earlier.

title: Dell patches critical 9.9 flaw in Enterprise SONiC
text:
A critical argument injection vulnerability in Dell Enterprise SONiC allows low-privileged remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands on network switches.

Dell Technologies has released a patch for CVE-2026-103782, a critical vulnerability in Dell Enterprise SONiC Distribution. The flaw, assigned a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.9, is classified as an argument injection issue that permits a low-privileged remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands and access unauthorised filesystem resources. Dell disclosed the advisory on 19 November 2026, noting that the vulnerability affects software versions prior to 4.6.1.

According to Dell’s severity rating, the flaw has low attack complexity and does not require user interaction, though it is not currently listed by CISA as known exploited. The advisory identifies several affected PowerSwitch platforms, including the E3200-ON series, N3200-ON, S3248T-ON, and S5248F-ON. Administrators are advised to verify the installed SONiC version on each device rather than relying solely on hardware model numbers, as the affected-products table may not cover every supported version.

Dell recommends upgrading affected systems to version 4.6.1, available via Dell My Account. Before applying the update, organisations should back up switch configurations and plan for service restoration in case of failure. title: Bots exploit leaked AWS keys in Docker images within eight seconds
text:
Researchers found that automated scanners identify and use credentials left in public container images almost instantly, highlighting a critical gap in registry security.

Researchers from Stony Brook University published 300 decoy Docker images containing fake AWS, OpenAI and Anthropic API keys across eight public registries, including Docker Hub, Amazon ECR and Red Hat Quay. The study revealed that bots, dubbed “ContainerBots”, located and used the AWS keys in under eight seconds, with the median time to first use being 51 seconds. Over four months, the decoy AWS keys received more than 140,000 API calls from over 5,000 IP addresses, while the OpenAI and Anthropic keys were drained of their entire balances.

The researchers observed that the bots do not run the containers; instead, they query registry catalogue endpoints for recently published images, download specific layers likely to contain credentials, and scan for key strings. This process takes only a few seconds. The study noted that Docker Hub’s pull counter lags actual downloads by five to six minutes, meaning image owners monitoring their pull counts cannot react before the credentials are already compromised. The authors stated that “publication and compromise are, for practical purposes, the same event.”

title: US investigates potential Iranian link in FortiGate breaches of 50 commercial ships
text:
US authorities are investigating whether Iranian state actors exploited known Fortinet FortiGate flaws to access the operational technology networks of up to 50 commercial vessels.

A US official told NPR that hackers exploited known flaws in Fortinet FortiGate devices used aboard vessels, with US intelligence estimating up to 50 commercial ships may have been compromised. The Wall Street Journal reported that the targeted ships carried oil, liquefied petroleum gas, chemicals, and other hazardous cargo, including at least one liquefied natural gas tanker. Authorities have not publicly attributed the breaches to Iran, and the figure remains an intelligence estimate rather than a confirmed count.

The FBI and US Coast Guard warned in September that attackers were exploiting FortiGate flaws in the maritime sector, specifically targeting unpatched devices. According to the US official, hackers moved from onboard information technology networks into operational technology systems that monitor and control physical equipment. While at least one ship experienced an extended communications blackout, the agencies stated there were no current reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental harm.

The investigation highlights the risk of connected business and control networks, where access to IT systems can provide a pathway to OT systems. Although reaching a ship’s control network does not prove that anyone took control of the vessel, i

title: Fake .NET job assessments used to spread malware via NuGet
text:
Researchers found 13 malicious NuGet packages disguised as coding assessments that steal credentials and establish remote access on Windows developer machines.

Socket researchers identified a coordinated supply-chain campaign targeting .NET developers with fake 'Home Assessment' projects. The campaign involves 13 malicious NuGet packages, primarily posing as button controls for WinUI 3 and WPF, which are designed to compromise Windows-based environments. According to the report, building or running these projects downloads files from GitHub, stages a DLL side-loading pair around the Microsoft On-Screen Keyboard (osk.exe), or executes a downloaded executable.

The attack leverages two malicious packages working in tandem: one executes code after every project build, while the other launches a staged executable when the application creates its button control. This mechanism turns routine development workflows into infection vectors. Socket traced the campaign across NuGet, GitHub repositories, and embedded malicious code, identifying four publisher accounts linked to the operation. The most recent example found was a GitHub repository created on 4 November 2026 containing a purported WinUI 3 assessment called 'Mini File Vault & Tracker'.

title: CISA adds Drupal, Idunno, and Optimizely flaws to KEV catalogue
text:
CISA has listed three actively exploited vulnerabilities, including a critical Drupal core flaw, in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue, setting a 27 November deadline for federal agencies.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogue on 24 November 2026. The list includes CVE-2026-132165, a critical remote code execution flaw in Drupal core; CVE-2026-131914, a critical deserialization vulnerability in the Idunno AntiCsrf library; and CVE-2026-132224, a high-severity issue in Optimizely Web Experimentation. Federal civilian agencies are required to address these flaws by 27 November 2026 under Binding Operational Directive 22-01.

CVE-2026-132165 allows an unauthenticated attacker to abuse the Drupal installation script, install.php, to reinstall the platform and gain full control of the website. The Drupal Security Team confirmed that attacks against live sites were reported as early as 19 November 2026. The flaw was discovered by Anthropic’s open-source software scanner. While restricting web server write access to settings.php blocks some attack paths, it does not mitigate all vectors.
