title: FinCEN takes systems offline after unauthorised access
text:
The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network has taken some systems offline as a precaution following a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorised access to a limited subset of its infrastructure.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) stated on 25 November 2026 that it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in "unauthorised access to a limited subset of its systems." As a proactive measure, the agency has taken some services offline, though it confirmed that the Bank Secrecy Act Electronic Filing (BSA E-Filing) System remains operational.

FinCEN, which collects suspicious activity reports and other Bank Secrecy Act filings from banks and other financial institutions, has extended deadlines for required document submissions. The agency advised that filers needing to expedite the delivery of suspicious activity information to law enforcement can use the Financial Institutions Hotline, which is not impacted by the service disruption.

This incident occurs while several other US federal agencies, including the FBI, the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, are reportedly investigating data breaches targeting criminal records and unclassified intelligence information.

title: GnuPG releases fix for critical GPGME memory corruption flaw
text:
A malicious OpenPGP key can trigger a double-free condition in GPGME, potentially allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or crash applications.

The GnuPG project has warned that a critical vulnerability in GPGME, the standard library used by programs to interface with GnuPG, could expose application data. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, is triggered by a malicious OpenPGP key containing an unusually long user ID.

According to the National Vulnerability Database, the bug arises when processing crafted input, where an early return following memory reallocation leaves internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory. This results in a double-free condition during cleanup, which a remote attacker could exploit to corrupt process memory, leading to arbitrary code execution or a denial-of-service crash.

The GnuPG project stated that fixed versions have been released. The vulnerability affects all software that uses GPGME prior to version 2.3.0. CISA has not listed this vulnerability in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.

title: CERT-In warns of AI-assisted attacks causing unauthorised payments
text:
India's CERT-In has issued an advisory stating that AI-assisted cyber attacks are targeting ICT assets, resulting in unauthorised financial transactions at banking and fintech entities.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has warned that threat actors are conducting artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cyber attacks against information and communication technology (ICT) assets within the country.

According to the advisory, this unsanctioned activity has led to unauthorised financial transactions at banking and financial services entities, as well as technology service providers.

The report highlights the use of AI in these operations, which has facilitated the execution of these unauthorised payments.

title: Critical ScreenConnect flaw exploited to hijack MSP technician PCs
text:
Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-84869 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to execute malicious payloads on technician hosts, bypassing standard session controls.

Security researchers have observed threat actors exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical vulnerability in the ConnectWise ScreenConnect client. The flaw allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician’s host without authorisation or host confirmation. According to The Hacker News, this activity targets managed service provider (MSP) servers, with one incident observed on 12 November 2026.

The National Vulnerability Database (NVD) describes the issue as a condition in the ScreenConnect client that permits unauthorised file transfer and execution through an active remote session. The vulnerability carries a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.9. CISA has listed the CVE in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalogue, noting it was added on 11 September 2026.

Crucially, the NVD record specifies that ScreenConnect servers are not impacted by this specific flaw. The risk is confined to the client-side interaction where a technician connects to a remote session.

title: Critical code injection flaw in binary-parser library
text:
A critical vulnerability in the binary-parser library allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript by manipulating parser definitions.

A critical code injection vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814, has been disclosed in the binary-parser library. The flaw affects versions prior to 2.3.1 and carries a CVSS 4.0 base score of 9.2.

According to the National Vulnerability Database, the vulnerability allows attackers who control parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption(). Attackers can supply crafted values for length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() aliases to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled.

CISA has listed the vulnerability as not currently known to be exploited in the wild.

title: US lawmakers propose CISA board to review major cyber incidents
text:
A new bill seeks to establish a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board within CISA to analyse root causes of significant cyber incidents without assigning liability.

Representatives Morgan Luttrell (R-TX) and Ritchie Torres (D-NY) introduced the ROOT CAUSE Act on 18 November, proposing the establishment of a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board (NCAI Board) within the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).

According to Infosecurity Magazine, the board would examine significant cyber incidents affecting US organisations, identify root causes, and recommend preventive measures. The legislation specifies that the NCAI Board would have no regulatory or enforcement authority, and its reviews would not assign civil or criminal liability.

The bill, introduced through House Homeland Security Republicans, was one of four new proposals on 18 November. The others include the AI INSIGHT Act for securing AI agents on federal networks, the BRIDGE AI Act for recruiting private-sector AI specialists to CISA, and the SECURE IT Act, which would designate the Department of Homeland Security as the Sector Risk Management Agency for the Information Technology Sector.

title: VMware 0-Day and Java4Shell featured in weekly security recap
text:
The Hacker News highlights a week of critical vulnerabilities including a VMware zero-day and Java4Shell, illustrating how small openings lead to major breaches.

The Hacker News has published a weekly recap detailing several significant security incidents, including a VMware zero-day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, and Ruby2Shell. The report emphasises that attackers often exploit existing trust or routine processes rather than forcing entry, noting that a single breach can facilitate access to other targets.

The publication describes how small security openings can rapidly escalate into larger compromises. It highlights the reliance on tools and trusted messages as vectors for these attacks, warning that routine updates or stolen keys can serve as the starting point for major security problems.

The recap notes that attackers do not always need to break down a door, sometimes using one that is already open, as these elements are frequently leveraged to turn a small opening into a much bigger mess.

title: Trump to nominate Kirsten Davies as US National Cyber Director
text:
The White House intends to appoint the Pentagon’s chief information officer to the role permanently following strong industry support.

President Donald Trump intends to nominate Kirsten Davies, the Department of Defense’s chief information officer, as the next National Cyber Director, according to a White House official. Davies was named acting director last week after the departure of Sean Cairncross. The decision follows what the official described as “overwhelming” support from industry and government leaders.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve in the role while Davies awaits Senate confirmation. Clayton stated that Davies has the “experience and capabilities needed to help America navigate our increasingly complex and powerful digital infrastructure.”

Davies previously served as chief information security officer at Unilever and Estée Lauder, and held security leadership roles at Barclays Africa, Hewlett Packard, Siemens, Booz Allen Hamilton, and Deloitte Australia. The appointment comes amid reports that the FBI’s National Crime Information Center has been hacked, following a major cyberattack in September that exposed personal information of FBI agents and Justice Department staffers.

title: Bots spoof AI agent names to hunt for secrets
text:
Cequence telemetry shows malicious bots have increasingly used AI agent names as cover to probe for secrets, while agents have moved from reading to signing in, booking and buying.

Security firm Cequence reported that malicious bots have adopted AI agent names as cover to probe for configuration files, keys and admin consoles. In its Agentic AI Security Index, published on 23 November, Cequence detailed telemetry collected between 16 May and 15 November 2026. Bot traffic using these identities climbed from fewer than 30 visits a day in May to a peak of approximately 1,450 in mid-October, with Cequence blocking 37,917 such visits over the period.

The report notes a shift in agent behaviour: among established AI agents, 13% of visits involved taking action in November, up from 1.4% in May. Action-taking visits, which include signing in, booking and buying, grew by 240%, while read-only visits fell by 73%. Cequence cautioned that agent names are self-reported and open to any bot, meaning the data does not implicate specific vendors like Perplexity, where 63% of claimed agent visits were probing for secrets.

Dana Simberkoff, chief risk, privacy and information security officer at AvePoint, stated that organisations need least-privilege access, identity controls and human approval for high-risk actions. Aviv Nahum, co-founder and CEO at Above Security, added that organisations must treat AI agents as "first-class identities and a new class of insiders." Cequence recommended gov

title: China-linked actor uses AI agents to exploit zero-day in 11 minutes
text:
Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a China-nexus actor used Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a zero-day in a medical imaging app, gaining root access in 11 minutes.

Researchers at Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a campaign running for approximately 48 hours from 8 September, targeting universities in East Asia outside mainland China. The actor, described as China-linked, deployed Cairn AI agents with the goal of obtaining shell access. The agents conducted two extensive autonomous operations that failed, including a 16-hour attempt to control an exposed Redis instance and a brute-force attack on a GPU server where the agents unsuccessfully tested more than 30,000 credential combinations.

The agents eventually targeted an exposed open source medical imaging application. By mapping API endpoints and testing a filename parameter for path traversal, they identified a zero-day vulnerability. According to CJ Moses, CISO of AWS, the agents went from mapping the application to writing files on the server in about 11 minutes, subsequently executing a Python reverse shell payload as root.

Security experts note that while machine-speed exploitation is not new, the absence of skilled human direction changes the economics of vulnerability discovery. Defenders are advised to apply fundamental security practices, such as monitoring for suspicious uploads and reviewing code, at automated speeds to counter these persistent, AI-driven operations.

title: Webworm suspected of modifying SoftEther VPN to evade detection
text:
A China-aligned threat actor is suspected of using a customised SoftEther VPN Bridge to hide remote access and bypass security tools.

The Hacker News reports that the China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected of deploying a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool. The group is suspected of modifying the software to remove recognizable detection fingerprints and disguise it as network-monitoring software, thereby establishing covert remote access to compromised networks.

According to the report, the modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools." This activity highlights the risk of open-source utilities being repurposed by state-aligned actors to maintain persistent access while evading standard defensive measures.

title: Serial-to-IP gateways broadcast lack of authentication to internet
text:
Research by Flare reveals that a significant proportion of exposed OT serial gateways publicly report that authentication is disabled, creating a direct path for attackers to access industrial machinery.

Adrian Cheek, senior cybercrime researcher at Flare, conducted an internet scan using a specific vendor's UDP discovery service and identified 2,474 serial-to-IP gateways exposed on the web. According to the report, these devices appeared to be real hardware rather than honeypots, with half located in Russia. When probed, approximately half of the devices responded by disclosing their authentication status. Of those that responded, 973 reported that authentication was disabled, meaning 39.3% of all exposed gateways visibly lacked authentication, and 77% of those whose status could be determined were unprotected.

Cheek noted that these devices often ship with authentication off and are configured by integrators who then leave them unattended for 10 to 15 years. Operators may avoid enabling security features because older SCADA packages and virtual serial port drivers may not support secured modes, risking the loss of the link to the field. Furthermore, firmware updates at remote sites carry the risk of breaking functionality if no spare hardware is available, leading operators to avoid touching working devices.

title: WHMCS SQL injection flaw exposes customer data and admin hashes
text:
An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in WHMCS allows attackers to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from the platform's database.

WHMCS has disclosed a SQL injection vulnerability in its shopping cart component, which is widely used by web hosting companies for billing and automation. The flaw permits any user on the internet to access the installation's database without requiring a login.

According to The Hacker News, the vulnerability could allow the retrieval of customer records and administrator password hashes. The company disclosed this issue alongside two other flaws that require a logged-in client to exploit.

Security professionals should note that while the primary flaw is unauthenticated, the other two disclosed vulnerabilities require valid client credentials. Organisations using WHMCS should verify their patch status immediately to prevent data exfiltration.

title: Ox Security: Agent instructions are a new AI attack path
text:
Analysis of 542,207 components shows prompt injection and tool poisoning are prevalent in MCP servers and agent skills, bypassing traditional code-based security checks.

Ox Security has warned that threat actors are hijacking AI agents through instructions rather than malicious code. The vendor’s 'Plug and Pray' report, based on an analysis of 542,207 open source components between July and October 2026, found that prompt injection and tool poisoning are more prevalent in certain ecosystems than traditional malware.

In Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, 22% of flagged components contained prompt injection or tool poisoning, while 16% executed code at install or import time. In agent skills, the disparity was wider: 26% contained such techniques, compared to 0% with install-time execution. Additionally, 44% of agent skills contained instructions directing agents to exfiltrate data. Neatsun Ziv, CEO of Ox Security, stated that companies are relying on trust signals built for a different era, noting that the issue is who controls the tool and what instructions it gives the agent.

The report highlights that traditional software trust models are failing. Ox Security found a source owner for only 70% of MCP servers, compared to 93% of npm packages. Furthermore, 67% of MCP servers ran on publisher-controlled infrastructure, making independent code verification impossible, and 82% were malicious in their first observed version, leaving no clean baseline for comparison.

title: Single-bit .NET change bypasses Windows code integrity
text:
A researcher demonstrated how a minor file alteration allows local attackers to execute untrusted code, bypassing Windows protections and VirtualBox hardening.

James Forshaw, a Google Project Zero researcher, published a write-up detailing how a quirk in the .NET Framework's file loading process allows a local attacker to run untrusted code. This behaviour bypasses two separate Windows code integrity protections designed to block such execution.

The same loading mechanism also circumvents process hardening in Oracle VirtualBox on Windows hosts. This specific bypass is tracked as CVE-2026-87268, affecting the Core component of Oracle VM VirtualBox version 7.2.16. The vulnerability is rated with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 7.8, indicating high severity for low-privileged local attackers.

According to the National Vulnerability Database, the vulnerability is easily exploitable and can result in the takeover of the VirtualBox instance. It applies exclusively to Windows hosts. CISA has not listed this vulnerability in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.

title: Attackers bypass GitHub SHA pinning via malicious Trivy code
text:
Threat actors have demonstrated a method to circumvent SHA pinning in GitHub Actions by injecting malicious code into the Trivy scanner that mimics official checkout tools.

SHA pinning, the practice of pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, has become a standard defence against software supply chain attacks. However, attackers have identified a way to bypass this control. According to The Hacker News, this gap is the subject of a recent webinar explaining how to close the security hole.

In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code designed to appear as if it originated from GitHub's official checkout tool. The source notes that the attackers even labelled the malicious component.

title: Okta links ShinyHunters-associated vishing group to new INCEPTION data leak site
text:
Okta Threat Intelligence assesses that a ShinyHunters-associated cluster may have rebranded as INCEPTION, continuing vishing attacks to harvest credentials and approvals.

Okta’s Threat Intelligence team has assessed that a threat cluster, designated O-UNC-053, previously affiliated with the ShinyHunters extortion crew, may have rebranded as INCEPTION. The group is characterised by the use of voice phishing (vishing) attacks to deceive targets into entering credentials on phishing pages and approving malicious actions.

According to Okta, this activity is linked to a new data leak site operating under the INCEPTION name. The assessment suggests the cluster has continued its operations under the new identity rather than ceasing activity.

title: FCA warns financial firms on AI agent security risks
text:
The UK Financial Conduct Authority has issued guidance requiring senior managers to oversee AI agent deployments, warning that failure to manage associated risks could lead to regulatory sanctions.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published guidance on 24 November 2026, stating that financial services firms must address cybersecurity risks arising from the deployment of AI agents. The regulator noted that these systems are increasingly used to initiate transactions and make investment decisions, which can blur the boundary between regulated and unregulated activity. Without appropriate safeguards, such as strict access controls, agents have been observed gaining access to sensitive systems and data, even when pursuing legitimate aims.

The FCA emphasised that responsibility for complying with regulatory obligations remains with senior managers and the organisation as a whole, whether the firm deploys agentic AI itself or relies on a third-party provider. Senior managers must take "reasonable steps" to understand the risks, provide effective oversight, and ensure governance controls and escalation arrangements are appropriate. Firms are also expected to help consumers understand the limits of AI-generated financial advice through clear disclaimers.

The authority stated it will assess services provided through agentic products to ensure they meet regulatory requirements. Failure to adhere to existing rules, including data protection laws, may result in the FCA using its

title: AI-assisted campaign compromises Check Point management servers
text:
GreyNoise reports a threat actor used AI-enabled tools to exploit and maintain persistent access to Check Point Security Management servers across multiple sectors.

Threat intelligence firm GreyNoise has identified a campaign, tracked as GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13), targeting Check Point Security Management servers. The actor, active since early October, used 99 IP addresses, many associated with disposable infrastructure or compromised victim devices, to conduct scanning, exploitation, and control activities. GreyNoise believes the actor employed agentic harnesses to weaponise vulnerabilities and automatically exploit assets, complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity.

The campaign targeted at least 22 organisations in the energy, financial services, government, and manufacturing sectors across the US, UK, Australia, and other geographies. In one instance, the actor forged a signed admin session cookie to gain administrative access to a Rejetto HFS server, subsequently obtaining SSH access to scan the environment and exfiltrate data. The attacker used one victim’s server as a relay to store command results and data exfiltrated from 24 previously compromised Check Point servers.

Between 20 and 26 October, the actor issued a bulk certificate-management task to 24 servers. Although the task failed, the actor collected responses containing victim IP addresses in incrementing order, indicating an automated loop. title: CISA warns of exploited N-able Mail Assure bug
text:
Federal agencies must patch a critical vulnerability in N-able's email security platform by Thanksgiving after it was exploited to breach company servers.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has directed federal departments to patch CVE-2026-134624, a vulnerability in N-able’s Mail Assure platform, by Thanksgiving. The bug, which carries a severity score of 9.3, was added to CISA’s exploited vulnerabilities platform on Monday evening.

N-able reported that hackers breached one of its servers through this vulnerability, causing a week of outages and damage to Mail Assure and SpamExperts services. The company stated it remediated the bug over the weekend and restored access to internal customer dashboards, while noting that inbound and outbound email flow and spam filtering continued to operate throughout the incident.

A N-able spokesperson said the company hired incident responders to validate its findings and has found no evidence of exploitation beyond the single N-able-hosted server identified in its initial investigation. The firm pledged to publish a root cause analysis within two weeks and clarified that this breach is not connected to more than 30 vulnerabilities in its N-central platform disclosed by a security researcher two weeks ago.

title: Iran-aligned Volant Manticore uses IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor
text:
A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group has targeted telecommunications, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus using a new IPFS-based backdoor.

The Hacker News reports that a group identified as Volant Manticore, described as Iran-aligned, has conducted espionage campaigns against telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus. The group’s operations rely on a backdoor named KuboShell, which utilises the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for command-and-control (C2) communications.

According to the report, KuboShell deploys Homa, a post-compromise framework described as a reimplementation of an existing tool. The article notes that the group and its tooling were previously undocumented, highlighting a new threat vector for defenders monitoring C2 traffic.

title: FulcrumSec claims 9.9 TB exfiltration from Gingko Bioworks
text:
FulcrumSec claims to have exfiltrated 9.9 TB of data from Gingko Bioworks Holdings, a breach the company acknowledged in October but has not since updated.

Gingko Bioworks Holdings issued a statement on 8 October acknowledging a data breach. According to DataBreaches.net, obtaining further updates from the company has been difficult since that initial disclosure.

On or about 19 November, the threat actor FulcrumSec added Gingko Bioworks Holdings to its clear net leak site. The group claims to have acquired 9.9 TB of data in total, comprising 10,775,976 files across 82 buckets. FulcrumSec provided detailed analysis of the acquired data on the leak site, though the victim has not confirmed these specific figures.

title: Lawmakers warn ID verification companies to bolster security after IDScan breach
text:
A bipartisan group of US federal lawmakers has written to identity verification companies, citing the IDScan breach that exposed over 150 million scanned IDs and pressing firms to provide detailed answers on data management.

Six US federal lawmakers, including Senators Brian Schatz and Marcia Blackburn, sent a letter to several identity verification firms on Monday, urging them to improve security practices following the September breach of IDScan. The incident resulted in the theft of customer data stored in the company’s cloud platform, leading to the exposure of scans for more than 150 million people’s drivers’ licenses and other identification documents, which subsequently appeared for sale on the dark web.

The letter highlights the risks of fraud and identity theft, noting that foreign adversaries can infer Americans’ behaviour through commercial data linked to government credentials. It specifically mentions that the exposed data included scans belonging to high-ranking military and intelligence officials, as well as nearly 600,000 medical cards and employment authorisations. The lawmakers stated that the scale of the breach warrants additional attention to the data-handling practices of these companies.

Independent journalist Brian Krebs, who first reported the IDScan breach, noted that cybercriminals on the Russia-tied dark web marketplace Nexus began exfiltrating the data more than a year before officials discovered it. Krebs also reported that many identity verif

title: Critical 'God Mode' flaws found in six countries' border systems
text:
Independent researcher Eaton Zveare discovered critical API vulnerabilities in the online visa and immigration systems of Nigeria, Ethiopia, Fiji, Zambia, Sri Lanka, and Ghana, allowing unauthorised access to sensitive data and administrative controls.

Security researcher Eaton Zveare identified critical API vulnerabilities, including broken object-level authorisation (BOLA), broken function-level authorisation (BFLA), and missing authentication, in the online passport and border-control systems of six nations. The flaws, which he described as 'God mode at the border,' allowed unauthorised access to millions of travellers' sensitive visa and passport data, potentially including biometric information such as fingerprints. In some cases, the vulnerabilities granted access to administrative functions that could be used to approve or deny entry into a country.

Zveare stated that the systems were built by third-party contractors with varying levels of expertise, which likely contributed to the security gaps. In Nigeria's case, he noted that an over-reliance on AI to build the systems may have introduced flaws into the code. He discovered the initial vulnerability in Nigeria's private back-end portal by searching Microsoft Bing for 'admin panel' approximately a year ago, before expanding his investigation to five other countries using similar web technologies such as Angular and React.

title: Rackspace shuts down Spot platform after Kubernetes breach
text:
Rackspace is permanently shutting down its Spot cloud platform after a breach allowed attackers to access customer Kubernetes clusters and secrets, forcing users to migrate by 8 December.

Rackspace has announced it will discontinue the Rackspace Spot cloud platform following a security incident that compromised customer environments. The company stated that it made the decision to wind down the service to provide a clear path forward for customers after reviewing the situation. The platform, which allows organisations to deploy and manage containerised applications using Kubernetes, will be permanently discontinued on 8 December 2026 at 5 pm Central Time, at which point all remaining workloads will be terminated and customer data will no longer be accessible.

According to Rackspace, hackers breached the Spot platform on 17 November using compromised credentials. This allowed them to create unauthorised pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes. The intrusion was discovered on 18 November following a customer report, leading Rackspace to disable access to the platform’s administration console. Service was restored on 21 November after an extended outage, though the company noted that an unauthorised party may have read cluster Secrets and files on storage volumes.

title: Webworm APT deploys custom SoftEther VPN to evade detection
text:
Rapid7 identified a modified SoftEther VPN tool used by the China-aligned Webworm group to maintain stealthy access to government networks.

Rapid7 published research on 19 November 2026 detailing a custom tool used by Webworm, a China-aligned advanced persistent threat group active since at least 2017. The group, also tracked as Erudite Mogwai and Space Pirates, primarily targets government organisations in Europe. The new tool, internally named "NtMonitor", is a modified build of the open source SoftEther VPN Bridge compiled for Windows x64.

According to Rapid7 researcher Milan Spinka, the attackers methodically analysed SoftEther's detection surface to implement counter-measures. The tool strips out standard artifacts, changes metadata to refer to generic "Network Monitor Software", and renames internal strings, HTTP endpoints, and handshake watermarks. Additionally, the core file hamcore.se2 is embedded inside the executable, and the plaintext configuration file is renamed and encrypted with a custom cipher to evade standard detection signatures.

Rapid7 attributed the software to Webworm with moderate confidence based on alignment with previously reported tactics, techniques, and procedures, as well as remote IP addresses linked to past Webworm activity. The research includes indicators of compromise and YARA rules for defenders. One of Webworm's primary initial access methods appears to be exploiting vulnerabilities through external web-facing applications.

title: ShinyHunters account posts on Exploit claiming future activity
text:
A post signed with the original ShinyHunters PGP key on the Exploit platform suggests further operations are planned, though the key's prior leak limits its evidentiary value.

A user posting on the Exploit platform yesterday used an account associated with the 2020 ShinyHunters group. The post allegedly explains recent events and outlines future actions, according to DataBreaches.net.

The message was signed with the group's original PGP key. However, the source notes that this signature does not definitively prove authenticity, as it had been reported months ago that the key had leaked.

The post also references additional details, though the provided source text is truncated and does not specify the full content of the claims.

title: WordPress removes six backdoored WP Connect plugins
text:
WordPress blocked six malicious plugin releases from WP Connect after a suspected developer account compromise enabled arbitrary code execution.

WordPress has removed six plugins developed by WP Connect following a suspected compromise of the developer's account on 22 November 2026. The compromised account was used to inject backdoors into the plugins, which would have enabled arbitrary code execution on any site with them installed.

The WordPress plugins team independently detected the threat and blocked the malicious releases before they could be officially published. Visiting the plugin listings now reflects the removal of these compromised versions.

title: Vinci RAT delivered via malicious Microsoft Store app
text:
Analysts identified a campaign using a legitimate Microsoft Store listing to install a backdoor that deploys Vinci RAT, allowing remote control of Windows systems.

eSentire’s Threat Response Unit documented an intrusion in early November 2026 where a user seeking a screenshot tool was redirected to a fake site serving a signed installer. This installer directed the user to 'Setup Assistant', a genuine Microsoft Store app published by ETPS Ltd, which acted as a backdoor. Unlike previous campaigns using fake storefronts, this attack leveraged a real store listing to establish trust.

Once installed, the app contacted a command-and-control server to monitor specific files and execute PowerShell or JavaScript commands. In the investigated case, this access launched a loader that retrieved Vinci RAT from a separate domain and created a Windows scheduled task running every 10 minutes to maintain persistence. The malware gathered system details and supported reverse shells, though not all capabilities were confirmed as used in the specific incident.

eSentire noted that Microsoft initially stated the app did not violate its terms after researchers reported it via the Store’s abuse form. The report does not confirm whether the listing was subsequently removed. The package metadata indicated a release date of 1 June 2026, suggesting the app may have been available for five months prior to the investigation.

title: Remus Stealer deploys fake Google Sheets extension to intercept Gmail
text:
Researchers identified a new module in the Remus Stealer infostealer that installs a malicious Chrome extension to exfiltrate email contents from signed-in users.

Gen Digital’s Gen Threat Labs identified a new component in the Remus Stealer malware that silently installs a fake Google Sheets extension in Google Chrome. The module, a 64-bit Windows DLL, alters local Chrome profile settings to register the add-on and enable Developer Mode, allowing it to read new emails from compromised Windows computers.

The extension polls for unread mail approximately once a minute across up to ten account slots, sending the sender, subject, message body, and victim’s email address to an attacker-controlled server. While Remus developers claimed on underground forums that the feature could maintain access after password changes, researchers found no evidence it exploits a Gmail zero-day; it relies on the victim remaining signed in to the browser session.

Invoke RE identified the fake add-on as version 0.5.4, noting it borrows the description of the legitimate Google Docs Offline extension but contains no spreadsheet interface. Although the code identifies attachment filenames, researchers did not observe the extension transmitting the files themselves, though message bodies may still contain sensitive data such as password reset links or sign-in codes.

title: AI-driven campaign compromises 24 Check Point management servers
text:
GreyNoise has identified a suspected AI-assisted intrusion campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers across 22 organisations in the financial, energy, and government sectors.

An unknown threat actor is using artificial intelligence-driven offensive tooling in a campaign tracked by GreyNoise as GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13). The activity has resulted in the compromise of 24 Check Point Security Management servers, impacting 22 distinct organisations globally.

According to The Hacker News, the intrusion activity is assessed to have targeted organisations in the financial services, energy, and government sectors. The report notes the use of AI-driven tooling in the offensive operations, though specific technical details regarding the exploitation method are not provided in the source text.

GreyNoise is monitoring the activity under the GT13 moniker. The campaign represents a significant risk to security infrastructure, as the compromise of management servers can potentially allow attackers to bypass perimeter defences and access internal networks.

title: US investigates suspected cyberattacks on up to 50 commercial ships
text:
US authorities are investigating a wave of cyber intrusions and intimidation campaigns targeting vessels carrying hazardous cargo, with Iran and Russia under scrutiny.

According to a Wall Street Journal report, US officials believe as many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum gas, and chemicals may have been targeted. The investigation focuses on suspected state-sponsored activity, with Iran emerging as the primary suspect, although a Trump administration official told the WSJ that investigators have found no evidence linking Iran to the incidents and described four of the attacks as minor disruptions.

The incidents reportedly involved both cyber intrusions and intimidation campaigns, including bomb threats and ransom demands. The US Coast Guard has deployed specialised cyber protection teams to at least four vessels approaching US ports, including the VL Prosperity and Kohaku, to investigate suspected compromises of their onboard networks. One vessel, the Vivit Africa, experienced system problems and received a bomb threat while transporting LNG from the US to Italy, though it is not established that a cyberattack caused the technical incident.

Attackers are reportedly exploiting vulnerabilities in Fortinet networking devices widely used in the maritime industry. title: Microsoft confirms NTLM auth failures after November updates
text:
November security updates for CVE-2026-118737 are causing authentication failures in third-party apps and devices that do not correctly implement NTLM message signing.

Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues following the installation of November security updates. These updates address CVE-2026-118737, a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime. The flaw stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely without user interaction on unpatched systems.

The November updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, designed to reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions establish a cryptographic session key. However, Microsoft stated in an updated support document that these improvements may cause authentication failures on patched devices, particularly affecting third-party apps, authentication proxy servers, single sign-on solutions, and application packaging tools that use NTLM.

Microsoft identified that affected devices often set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in their CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field. As a temporary workaround, the company advised setting the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm registry value to 1 under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0.
