title: Hex.pm RCE flaw exploited on six production servers
text:
An attacker executed operating system commands on six Hex.pm servers using a critical remote code execution vulnerability present since 2016.

According to The Hacker News, an attacker ran operating system commands on six production servers of Hex.pm, the package registry used by Elixir and Erlang developers to fetch dependencies. The incident occurred on Monday, exploiting a remote code execution flaw with a CVSS score of 10.0.

The vulnerability had been present in the registry's code since February 2016. The Hex.pm maintenance team responded rapidly, placing every server on a patched build within approximately 15 minutes of the first malicious request.

title: New Inception extortion gang linked to SSO vishing campaign
text:
Okta and ReversingLabs link a new data extortion group to a voice phishing operation targeting single sign-on credentials, with Okta assessing the cluster very likely changed its brand affiliation from ShinyHunters.

A newly formed data extortion group named Inception has been linked to a large-scale campaign targeting single sign-on (SSO) credentials of global brands. The group surfaced on 17 November, claiming seven victims on its extortion site, including AMD, PepsiCo, Cigna Healthcare, AutoZone, and Lucid Motors, though none have publicly confirmed a breach. ReversingLabs says the gang has been operating since late October, identifying 21 domains used for SSO phishing and 41 domains believed to be part of the campaign infrastructure.

The campaign relies on phone-based social engineering rather than email phishing, with callers posing as support staff to pressure employees into resetting passwords via fake sign-in pages. These pages, often mimicking Okta or NetIQ/OpenText Access Manager, capture credentials before seeking additional multifactor authentication factors. ReversingLabs noted the lure sites are web-only and use legal-themed lookalike domains, bypassing email filters entirely.

Okta linked the operators to threat cluster O-UNC-053, previously associated with the ShinyHunters extortion group. Okta assessed that the cluster "very likely changed their brand affiliation" after law enforcement disrupted ShinyHunters in September. Inception disputes this link, claimi

title: CISA flags exploited RCE in abandoned Idunno.AntiCsrf library
text:
Unauthenticated remote code execution in a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF module is being actively exploited, with no patch available for the defunct project.

CISA added CVE-2026-131914 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on 24 November 2026, alongside two other flaws. The vulnerability is a deserialization of untrusted data issue in Idunno.AntiCsrf, a legacy ASP.NET WebForms module. Mandiant warned on 18 November that active exploitation in the wild has been observed.

The bug allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code in the context of the IIS worker process by sending a specially crafted HTTP POST request. No prior authentication or valid CSRF token is required. WatchTowr reported that the vulnerable check runs before the application’s own page logic, meaning it can affect many pages on an affected site, not just those using login forms. Attackers have been observed using web redirects to validate exploitation on vulnerable systems.

Because the open-source project has not been updated since December 2008, a patch is unlikely to be released. Mandiant advised organisations to stop using Idunno.AntiCsrf and replace it with actively supported alternatives such as System.Web.Helpers.AntiForgery or ASP.NET Core Anti-Request Forgery. CISA has ordered US federal civilian agencies to address the vulnerability and check for signs of exploitation by 27 November.

title: Samsung Securities breach exposes 8,241 customer records
text:
Personal data including names, addresses, and account numbers for thousands of Samsung Securities customers has been exposed online following a reported data breach.

According to Times Now News, Samsung Securities has suffered a data breach that exposed the personal information of 8,241 customers. The incident reportedly involves the leakage of sensitive details, including customer names, home addresses, and account numbers.

The report notes that cyberattacks are rising globally, with artificial intelligence making it increasingly difficult for companies to protect customer data.

No further details regarding the specific attack vector or the timeline of the breach were provided in the source material.

title: Bluetooth flaws in Elecbrakes controllers allow remote brake manipulation
text:
Researchers demonstrated that unauthenticated attackers within 100 metres can engage or release trailer brakes, posing a severe physical safety risk.

Australian consultancy Element Digital identified three vulnerabilities in Bluetooth-enabled brake controllers manufactured by Elecbrakes. The flaws include two critical issues involving missing authentication and insufficient replay-attack protection, which allow an unauthenticated attacker within Bluetooth range (up to 100 metres) to manipulate braking force or engage/release brakes without victim interaction.

CISA published an advisory last week noting the affected units are primarily used in Australia and New Zealand. The researchers warned that forcing a trailer’s brakes to maximum while the tow vehicle continues moving could cause a jackknife, a highly dangerous accident scenario. A third medium-severity flaw in the firmware update mechanism could enable persistent compromise, though researchers noted this risk remains theoretical as they did not demonstrate full impact.

Elecbrakes released firmware patches for the EB2 and VM1 products in early July after being notified in mid-May. The vendor stated that 60–70% of daily active controllers have installed the update, which requires physical pairing for remote access. No evidence of malicious exploitation has been found, but the vendor is still developing a remediation plan for the older ELBC 2000 model.

title: UK NCSC reports marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks
text:
Britain's National Cyber Security Centre warns that AI agents are accelerating attacks on existing weaknesses, urging organisations to reinforce basic security controls.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) stated on Tuesday that it has observed a "marked rise" in cyberattacks assisted by artificial intelligence since September. The agency explained that while AI is not rendering established cybersecurity practices obsolete, it is reducing the margin for error for organisations that have failed to implement basic defences. The NCSC noted that these tools increase attackers' speed, scale, and persistence while lowering costs, largely due to the availability of hacking frameworks combined with cheap open models or illegal API resellers.

The blog post, co-authored by NCSC chief technology officer for architecture David Chismon, identified Artex as the predominant framework currently receiving attention. It also named Cairn, PentAGI, RedAmon, Xalgorix, and Darkmoon as other tools in use. The NCSC emphasised that the weaknesses being exploited are not new or novel, and that the tools provide no new capability beyond what typical threat actors already possess. However, compared with human attackers, these agentic frameworks work more quickly, are exhaustive in their searches, and learn instantly from failures.

NCSC chief executive Richard Horne warned that the threat is increasing because previously tolerated weaknesses can now be discovered and exploited at scale. Chi

title: Two unrelated database leaks expose 3.5 billion credentials
text:
Researchers found two separate databases containing billions of usernames, passwords, and identity documents left exposed to the public internet.

According to new findings shared with WIRED, two unrelated databases were left exposed to anyone online, containing more than 3.5 billion usernames, passwords, national identity numbers, and documents. The data was part of entries for the “No need to hack when it’s leaking” files, a collection of exposed data sets.

The leaks included personal data from a wide range of individuals, with the specific nature of the two databases described as unrelated. The exposure allowed unauthorised access to sensitive information, including credentials and identity documents, without the need for active exploitation of a software vulnerability.

title: Gleneagles Hospital HK suspends app after data breach
text:
Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong has suspended its patient mobile application following the detection of unauthorised access to sensitive personal data.

Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong stated that it detected unauthorised activity on 18 November involving security infrastructure supporting its My Gleneagles mobile application. The hospital subsequently suspended the app after confirming that personal data had been accessed without authorisation.

According to The Standard, the compromised data includes patients’ names, identity document numbers, and contact details. The hospital posted a statement on its website on Tuesday regarding the incident and the suspension of the service.

title: Carnegie Endowment donor data leaked via Soapbox Engage breach
text:
A cyberattack on third-party fundraising platform Soapbox Engage exposed donor contact details and giving history for the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace confirmed that a cyberattack on its third-party vendor, Soapbox Engage, resulted in the leakage of donor information. The incident occurred on 28 October, and the organisation stated that threat actors were removed from the vendor’s system on 30 October. Spokesperson Sharmeen Aly confirmed that the breach affected a small percentage of the database, exposing names, email addresses, phone numbers, and giving history, but no full credit card numbers.

Carnegie notified all individuals in its database regarding the breach, citing European data privacy laws, and hired a cybersecurity firm to verify the removal of the attackers. The incident coincides with recent security disclosures from other digital donation platforms, including DonorPerfect and GoFundMe. GoFundMe stated it identified two separate attacks in October and November, while The Nonprofit Times reported that these attacks on fundraising platforms appeared to be coordinated, with at least one incident involving the theft of funds.

Soapbox Engage did not respond to requests for comment. GoFundMe said it had disabled unauthorized accounts and is monitoring for further suspicious activity, noting that the recent attacks highlight the need for better protection of donor information across the sector.

title: Radware breach exposes customer cloud log export credentials
text:
An unauthenticated internal API exposed customer contact details and cloud storage keys, prompting Radware to advise immediate credential rotation.

Radware disclosed that an unauthorised party accessed an internal Cloud WAF management API on 19 November 2026. The API was reachable from the public internet without requiring authentication, allowing attackers to view customer contact details and, for a subset of customers, credentials configured for log export into self-managed storage such as AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or SFTP.

The company stated it detected the breach ten hours after the initial access and subsequently blocked the originating IP address and revoked internal account credentials. Radware confirmed that WAF traffic inspection, certificates, end-user data, and cloud DDoS services were not exposed, and that no changes to customer security policies were identified.

Radware has advised affected AppSec customers to rotate their Cloud WAF log export credentials immediately. The company also recommended reviewing access logs on cloud storage accounts for unexpected activity since 19 November, noting it has already received reports of AWS alerts regarding unfamiliar IP addresses attempting to access log-export buckets.

title: Turnitin detects unauthorized activity in customer-facing systems
text:
Educational technology firm Turnitin has disclosed a cyberattack affecting its customer-facing systems, with no confirmation yet of data theft or service disruption.

Turnitin disclosed that it detected unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems and subsequently deployed its incident response plan. According to a public statement from CEO Chris Caren, the company is investigating the incident with the assistance of external cybersecurity specialists. Law enforcement and cyber regulators have been notified of the breach.

The company stated that its systems remain fully operational and safe to use. Turnitin noted that the affected systems do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information. The firm has not disclosed the nature or scope of the unauthorized activity, nor whether any user data was accessed or stolen.

As of 24 November 2026, no ransomware groups have publicly claimed responsibility for the attack. Turnitin continues to monitor its systems for further unauthorized activity, acknowledging that it is too early to guarantee the threat has been eliminated. The company’s status page shows no incidents for November 2026, and uptime history logs no disruptions.

title: McDonald's Japan breach exposes app user location and purchase data
text:
McDonald's Japan confirmed a database breach affecting its official mobile app, exposing customer location data and purchase histories without revealing the scale of the incident.

McDonald's Japan disclosed on Friday that threat actors gained unauthorised access to a database associated with the company's official smartphone app. The company stated that the compromised data includes users' product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data, and customer management IDs. It confirmed that names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, and credit card information were not exposed.

The company has not disclosed when the intrusion was detected, how many individuals were affected, or who was responsible. McDonald's Japan said a follow-up investigation found no service disruption or misuse of the official apps as a result of the incident. It is currently working to invalidate credentials used for the unauthorised access and has reported the incident to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission.

This incident follows a wave of cyberattacks targeting Japanese organisations, including a recent breach at Burger King Japan. A researcher at Macnica noted that attackers are increasingly probing websites and APIs for access-control and authentication weaknesses, and exploiting known vulnerabilities to find other victims.

title: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach
text:
The European Commission confirmed that an AI-assisted cyberattack resulted in the compromise of user names and email addresses on its EU Academy platform.

The European Commission (EC) confirmed on 24 November 2026 that an investigation into a recent cyberattack uncovered a data breach affecting EU Academy, its online learning platform. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier stated that compromised information includes the names and email addresses of users, though the full extent of the breach remains under investigation. Access to the platform has been suspended, and the European Data Protection Supervisor has been notified.

The intrusion was detected on 22 October 2026 and involved the use of an AI-assisted tool. According to Euronews, the Commission suspects a China-backed threat group, a claim based partly on the use of Artex, an AI-powered penetration testing framework with Chinese roots. The EC declined to confirm attribution, stating it could only be made once the investigation is concluded. Euronews also reported that the attack has yet to be fully contained, despite the EC saying last week that it had largely been contained.

The Commission has published a notice on the EU Academy website warning users to be suspicious of unsolicited emails or messages that may be part of potential phishing attacks. Regnier noted that no direct outreach has been made to individual users yet, as the exact scale of the data leak is still subject to investigation.

title: Colorado shuts down myColorado app after data breach
text:
The state's digital ID and services app is offline after an unauthorised breach that may have exposed data for up to 150,000 users.

The Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) confirmed that the myColorado app was taken offline following a cyberattack discovered on the evening of 18 November. The app, which provides digital identification, document storage, and access to state government services, has 2.1 million registered users.

According to OIT, an unauthorised user accessed data on the app’s platform, and the attack likely involved the theft of information tied to nearly 150,000 individuals. Investigators have not disclosed the specific types of data compromised. Sarah Tuneberg, executive director of OIT, stated that protecting user data is the priority and systems will be restored once security is confirmed.

Colorado has urged residents to carry physical identification for travel during the Thanksgiving holiday. State services remain accessible via individual agency websites while the app remains unavailable.

title: Broadcom patches critical VMware ESX and vCenter flaws
text:
Broadcom has released cumulative updates for 23 vulnerabilities, including critical authentication bypass and code execution issues in VMware ESX and vCenter.

Broadcom announced on Tuesday that it has released patches for 23 vulnerabilities across multiple VMware products. The vCenter updates address seven bugs, most notably a critical authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service tracked as CVE-2026-123903, which carries a CVSS score of 9.8. The fixes also resolve three denial-of-service issues, a local privilege escalation in a vpxd service script, an arbitrary file write vulnerability, and a security policy enforcement failure in the vSphere Distributed Switch.

The ESX updates resolve seven security issues, including three critical-severity weaknesses that allow code execution on the host. CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911 are heap out-of-bounds write and use-after-free flaws in the I/O filter service, both rated 9.8. CVE-2026-123912 is an out-of-bounds write in the XHCI USB controller requiring local administrative privileges, rated 9.3. Broadcom noted that on ESX, exploitation is contained within the VMX sandbox, whereas on Workstation and Fusion, it may lead to code execution on the host machine.

Additional fixes cover eight flaws in Avi Load Balancer, which could lead to code execution with root privileges and privilege escalation, and one denial-of-service issue in VMware Tools. Broadcom stated that vCenter version 8.0 U3m already contains the fixes, so t

title: Drupal core RCE flaw exploited in the wild
text:
CISA and Drupal confirm active exploitation of CVE-2026-132165, a remote code execution vulnerability in the core installer patched on 18 November.

Drupal core vulnerability CVE-2026-132165 is being exploited in the wild, according to CISA and Drupal developers. The flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker to abuse the installer to reinstall Drupal, potentially hijacking the website or executing arbitrary code. Drupal’s security team stated that reports of exploitation on live sites began as early as 19 November 2026, shortly after the patch was released on 18 November.

The vulnerability was discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that scans enrolled open source projects. CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 24 November, instructing federal agencies to address it by 27 November. No public information is currently available regarding the scale of the attacks or the specific number of affected websites.

Drupal raised the vulnerability’s rating to 'highly critical' with a CMSS score of 20/25 upon learning of the attacks. This is the third Drupal vulnerability exploited in the wild this year, following CVE-2026-118539 in the Commerce Core module and CVE-2026-9082 reported in May.

title: Palo Alto patches Fragnesia flaw exploited to root firewalls
text:
Palo Alto Networks has released PAN-OS updates to address CVE-2026-46300, a Linux kernel vulnerability exploited in conjunction with PHP2Shell to gain root access on internet-exposed firewalls.

Palo Alto Networks announced on Tuesday that it has released PAN-OS updates to patch the Fragnesia Linux kernel vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-46300. Disclosed in May 2026, this privilege escalation bug in the kernel’s XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem allows unprivileged attackers to overwrite sensitive system files to gain root permissions.

According to SecurityWeek, cybersecurity firm Dream warned on 26 October that a Chinese-speaking threat actor successfully exploited the critical PHP2Shell bugs and the Fragnesia weakness to hack two servers of a US government-affiliated organisation. As part of the AI-assisted campaign, the attackers compromised 25 servers (24 firewalls and one internal firewall management server), exploiting PHP2Shell to gain remote code execution (RCE), and executing a Fragnesia exploit to deploy webshells with root privileges.

Palo Alto Networks confirmed on 29 October that the threat actor targeted PAN-OS firewalls with management interfaces exposed to the internet in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with Fragnesia. While the company released patches for PHP2Shell across all supported versions by 30 October, it now recommends applying the new Fragnesia fixes, noting that the only known way to exploit it against PAN-OS is to first exploit PHP2Shell via an internet-ex

title: CISA adds three actively exploited vulnerabilities to KEV Catalog
text:
CISA has listed three new vulnerabilities in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation that poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.

On 24 November 2026, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. The agency stated that these flaws are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

The additions include CVE-2026-131914, a critical deserialization flaw in Idunno AntiCsrf; CVE-2026-132165, a remote code execution vulnerability in Drupal Core; and CVE-2026-132224, a high-severity issue in Optimizely Web Experimentation. CISA noted that Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04 requires Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to prioritise rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities listed in the KEV Catalog, particularly those on publicly exposed assets that grant total control post-exploitation.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to federal agencies, CISA encourages all organisations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management. The agency advises checking whether threat actors compromised systems before patches were applied, as per the directive's expectations for federal entities.

title: CISA warns of heap overflow in AutomationDirect C-More EA9 software
text:
A heap-based buffer overflow in C-More EA9 Programming Software could allow arbitrary code execution if users open a malicious file.

CISA has issued an advisory for a vulnerability in AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-127280, is a heap-based buffer overflow that occurs when the software fails to adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations.

According to the advisory, a crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to corrupt application memory and cause a crash, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution. The attack vector requires a user to be convinced to open a malicious project file delivered through channels such as email, file sharing, or removable media.

The vulnerability affects C-More EA9 Programming Software versions up to and including V6.80. It carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 7.8 (High) and a CVSS v4.0 score of 8.4 (High). The vulnerability was reported to CISA by rgod of TrendAI Zero Day Initiative.

title: Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controller vulnerable to unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow
text:
CISA has issued an advisory for a critical stack-based buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controllers that hypothetically allows potential arbitrary code execution without authentication.

CISA has published an ICS advisory (ICSa-26-328-03) detailing a critical vulnerability in the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controller. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-129713, is a stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler. According to the advisory, remote attackers can send specially crafted HTTP/S POST requests to trigger memory corruption, causing the webserver to restart and hypothetically potentially allowing arbitrary code execution with webserver privileges.

The vulnerability carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8 (Critical) and a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.3. It was reported to CISA by Carlo Meijer of Midnight Blue. CISA notes that the vulnerability is not currently listed as known exploited. The affected product is deployed worldwide in commercial facilities, with Danfoss headquartered in Denmark.

Danfoss has stated that the vulnerability will be addressed in an upcoming software release for the AK-SM 800A Series, specifically version 5.5.x. Additionally, the vendor plans to remove the ability for users to disable Strict Mode in future releases. CISA recommends minimising network exposure for control system devices and ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.

title: Schneider Electric patches Rapsody software use-after-free flaw
text:
CISA has published an advisory for a use-after-free vulnerability in Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software that allows local code execution via malicious files.

Schneider Electric has identified a use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-119055) in its EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software. The flaw, classified as CWE-416, permits a local attacker to execute arbitrary code by tricking an end user into opening a specially crafted malicious SSD file.

The vulnerability affects multiple regional versions of the software, including French, Spanish, Portuguese, Belgian, international, and Dutch builds. According to the CISA advisory, failure to apply the remediations may risk memory corruption, heap-based buffer overflow, and/or stack-based buffer overflow.

The National Vulnerability Database lists the CVSS 4.0 base score as 4.6 (medium). CISA does not currently list this vulnerability as known exploited. Schneider Electric has released fixed versions for all affected regional builds.

title: Microsoft warns of potential printing failures for Forcepoint users after hotpatch
text:
The November 2026 Windows hotpatch may cause Print Spooler failures on Windows 11 24H2 systems running Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent.

Microsoft has confirmed a known issue affecting systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later that have installed the KB5132043 Windows hotpatch. The company stated that a compatibility issue between the update and the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent may cause the Print Spooler service to fail to start, resulting in greyed-out print options or errors when selecting a printer.

This issue is specific to devices managed via Microsoft's Windows Autopatch service, which deploys hotpatch updates. It does not affect systems that received the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates. Microsoft noted that the hotpatch is also causing installation and launch issues for Office and third-party applications on Windows 11 systems.

No fix is currently available from Microsoft. Forcepoint has published a temporary workaround in its support portal for affected customers. Microsoft previously warned that the standard November 2026 updates may also break printing for documents with complex formatting on Windows Server 2016 or later and Windows 10 or later devices.

title: Peruvian call centre operator jailed for $15m government impersonation fraud
text:
A Lima-based operator was sentenced to eight years for managing call centres that defrauded over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents.

Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza, a 45-year-old call centre operator from Lima, Peru, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud. According to court documents, she managed and operated Peruvian call centres linked to large-scale fraud and extortion schemes between January 2013 and December 2018.

The scheme targeted Spanish-speaking US residents, initially offering free services before impersonating US government officials and lawyers to demand payment. The Department of Justice stated that the operation defrauded more than 30,000 victims out of $15 million, using threats of court action, arrest, and immigration consequences. Alcedo was extradited to the United States in April 2025 following her arrest in March 2023.

This conviction is part of a broader enforcement effort; Alcedo is the tenth defendant extradited from Peru in this case. The US Federal Trade Commission reported in June 2026 that Americans lost $3.5 billion to impersonation scams in 2025, with approximately $920 million stolen by government impersonators.

title: NYSDFS settles $6.75m with Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper
text:
New York regulators announced settlements with two major mortgage lenders, highlighting the importance of effective multi-factor authentication controls and timely incident reporting.

The New York State Department of Financial Services (NYSDFS) announced on 19 November 2026 that Rocket Mortgage LLC and Nationstar Mortgage LLC d/b/a Mr. Cooper will pay a combined $6.75 million in cybersecurity settlements. Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow stated that the settlements highlight the importance of effective multi-factor authentication controls and timely incident reporting.

title: Cyberattack disrupts Guadeloupe university hospital IT systems
text:
A major cyberattack on Saturday night forced the Guadeloupe university hospital to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

According to RFI, a significant cyberattack disrupted the information and telephone systems of the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe. The incident occurred on Saturday night and left staff unable to access several applications and databases.

The disruption forced the hospital to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5m after API credential theft
text:
A cyberattack on B2B gift card distributor GlobeTopper resulted in $2.5m in lost revenue and the redemption of $70,000 in digital gift cards.

Parent company iQSTEL disclosed in a US Securities and Exchange Commission filing that it detected unauthorised activity at its subsidiary GlobeTopper on 22 October 2026. The company suspended its platform and took affected servers offline on 23 October to investigate the intrusion. A rebuilt platform was deployed on AWS on 31 October, with commercial operations restored in stages from 1 November.

According to iQSTEL, the attacker obtained API credentials and integration keys belonging to certain business customers. The company stated that all affected credentials have been revoked and rotated, and new credentials have been issued to affected customers with additional access restrictions. An investigation is ongoing to determine whether other customer, personal, payment, or provider data was accessed.

The incident caused an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue, while the attacker redeemed digital gift cards worth $70,000. GlobeTopper stated it cannot block, recover, or reclaim the redeemed cards and will incur the losses. No ransomware groups have listed iQSTEL or GlobeTopper as victims on their extortion portals.

title: LaLiga confirms cyberattack exposed fan personal data
text:
Spain's top football league disclosed that a cybercriminal accessed its fan services platform between 14 and 16 November, extracting personal data from registered users.

LaLiga, the organiser of Spain's top two men's professional football divisions, confirmed a data breach affecting users of its digital services and those of some affiliated clubs. The organisation stated that a cybercriminal gained unauthorised access to one of its technology platforms for fan services between 14 and 16 November 2026.

According to LaLiga, its security team identified the source of the unauthorised access on 16 November and implemented measures to block the attack and stop the data extraction. The incident was confined to the specific fan services platform and did not extend to other systems supporting the running of the competitions.

LaLiga reported the incident to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and filed a complaint with the National Police’s Central Cybercrime Unit. Impacted clubs were directly notified, and actions to inform affected fans are being coordinated. No ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the attack as of the time of writing.

title: RansomwareHelp CTO indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
text:
The co-founder of a firm claiming to decrypt ransomware without payment has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI operation revealed he was secretly paying attackers and charging victims a markup.

Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, the chief technology officer and co-founder of Florida-based RansomwareHelp, has been indicted for wire fraud in Rhode Island. The company, which operated for six years, advertised 'advanced cryptographic tools' that could restore 100% of data without paying ransoms, claiming a 99% success rate and a team of 80 experts. However, the indictment alleges that Palacio routinely paid ransomware groups for decryption keys and charged victims significantly more than the amount paid to the threat actors.

The FBI conducted a sting operation in which agents posed as both a ransomware victim and a fictitious ransomware group. When the fake victim contacted RansomwareHelp, the company reiterated its policy against paying ransoms. Shortly after, Palacio contacted the FBI’s fake ransomware group, negotiating a decryption key for approximately $6,000 in bitcoin. He then billed the fake victim $16,010, including a diagnostic fee and the decryption cost.

Paul Ihme, co-founder of security firm Soteria, described a 2024 incident where RansomwareHelp proposed a $438,880 recovery fee for a Lockbit infection, citing '510 preconfigured forensic servers' and 'brute force processes'. Ihme noted that RansomwareHelp insisted on remote access via Anydesk, which he believes

title: CISA adds MONAI Label and Mail Assure flaws to KEV Catalog
text:
CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, citing active exploitation of a path traversal flaw in MONAI Label and an SSRF issue in N-able Mail Assure.

CISA announced on 23 November 2026 that it has added two vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. The first is CVE-2026-133968, a path traversal vulnerability in Project MONAI MONAI Label that allows remote code execution via the image parameter to the PUT /datastore/image endpoint. The NVD records indicate this flaw has been exploited in the wild since September 2026 and carries a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8 (critical).

The second addition is CVE-2026-134624, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in N-able Mail Assure (SpamExperts). According to the NVD, the software fails to restrict the destination of the LDAP synchronisation connection check when a relay is configured. An authenticated API user can exploit this to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine reachability, and send crafted data to internal services. This vulnerability has a CVSS 4.0 base score of 9.3 (critical).

CISA stated that these types of vulnerabilities are frequent attack vectors for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are required to prioritise rapid remediation of high-risk vulnera

title: Verizon report: Credential abuse drives 13% of breaches
text:
Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report identifies credential abuse as the initial access vector in 13% of breaches.

According to BleepingComputer, Verizon’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found that credential abuse was the initial access vector in 13% of breaches. The report also noted that vulnerability exploitation accounted for 31% of breaches. These findings underscore the continued reliance on compromised or weak credentials for unauthorised access to corporate systems.

The article highlights that manual tracking methods, such as spreadsheets, often fail to capture the full scope of an organisation's credentials. It notes that employees frequently store passwords in browsers, chat messages, or personal vaults due to convenience, creating blind spots for administrators. Verizon’s 2025 report, cited in the text, indicated that in the median case, only 49% of users’ passwords were unique across services, with 123456 identified as the most common corporate password by NordPass.

Ransomware groups, such as Pysa, are reported to use automated scripts to scan drives for files containing terms like “password” or “login.” If attackers locate such documents, they may encrypt them or use the contained credentials to access other accounts, potentially spreading the attack further. The source advises that organisations require structured approaches to manage credential visibility, strength, and ownership.

title: Michigan nurse jailed for $1.6m Medicare fraud using stolen records
text:
A home health care owner was sentenced to four years in prison for billing Medicare for services that were never performed, using stolen patient data.

Ruby Scott, a nurse from Farmington Hills, Michigan, was sentenced to four years in federal prison on Thursday. She owned and operated Delta Home Health Care LLC.

According to a press release from the Justice Department, Scott used stolen patient records to bill Medicare for fake services. The total value of the fraud scheme was reported as $1.6 million.

title: Austrian Foreign Ministry website breached, diplomat contacts exposed
text:
A breach of an external website exposed official contact details for Austrian diplomats, with no attribution yet made.

Austria's Foreign Ministry confirmed that hackers breached one of its websites between 12 and 13 November, accessing the names and official contact information of employees at its Vienna headquarters and diplomatic missions abroad. The incident affected a website operated by an external service provider, and the ministry stated that the breach has been contained.

The ministry said no personal information belonging to members of the public was compromised. It has notified Austria's cybersecurity and data protection authorities but has not disclosed specific technical vulnerabilities or security measures for security reasons. The attack coincided with a global Microsoft service outage, though Austrian authorities have not established a link between the two incidents.

There is no public evidence linking Russia to this latest cyberattack, despite the ministry having been targeted by suspected state-sponsored hackers linked to Moscow in 2019 and 2020. Vienna publicly attributed that earlier attack to Russia in July 2026, amid worsening diplomatic relations following the expulsion of Russian diplomats and a drone strike on the Austrian Embassy in Kyiv.

title: Human Security disrupts BadBox 3.0 ad fraud botnet
text:
The third iteration of the BadBox operation generated 40 billion daily bid requests by spoofing CTV apps on low-cost Android devices.

Bot and fraud protection firm Human Security says it has disrupted BadBox 3.0, the largest ad fraud botnet by bid volume. At its height, the operation accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform, a volume three times that of the VastFlux scheme.

The botnet targets low-cost, uncertified Android Open Source Project devices infected with backdoors. These devices run fraud modules that render hidden video ads in a background window, mimicking legitimate video ad SDKs to make bid requests appear to come from known applications. The threat actors also use server-side ad insertion to monetise this application spoofing.

Human Security’s Satori Threat Intelligence and Research Team linked the operation to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ, noting that modules check for TXCZ build properties and a TXCZ domain serves payload downloads. The firm also identified an actively maintained catalogue of fraud modules on public repositories, including residential proxy modules that enrolled devices into eleven networks, including PXYEDGE.

title: Dragos finds prompt theft at three AI inference providers
text:
Threat actors stole customer prompts and credentials from at least three AI inference providers, with none detecting the intrusions until notified by researchers.

Cybersecurity firm Dragos reported that threat actors breached at least three AI inference providers and stole customer prompts, but none of the victims detected the intrusions until they were notified. The discovery followed a test where a team led by Dragos chief research officer HD Moore sent roughly two million prompts containing unique bait, such as URLs, hostnames, and AWS keys, to widely used AI services between July and November.

Moore stated that the bait prompts were processed alongside real customer requests, which were "almost certainly copied too". The largest breach involved roughly 200 AWS test keys stolen in late October. Dragos observed the attackers checking which stolen keys worked and attempting to use them to obtain valuable data from associated accounts. The firm noted that some stolen keys came from requests rejected before a model ran, indicating the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door rather than deeper in the inference stack.

OpenRouter, an AI gateway, said its own systems were not breached but removed three unnamed providers in response. Phala admitted that requests sent between 21 October and 8 November should be considered exposed after an attacker compromised a server running a DeepSeek model. Together AI revealed that an AI coding agent leaked credentials on G

title: Peninsula Energy warns of disruption after Wyoming cyber incident
text:
An Australian-listed energy company has requested a trading halt to investigate a cybersecurity breach at its uranium project in Wyoming.

Peninsula Energy stated that a cybersecurity incident at its Lance uranium project in Wyoming would temporarily affect operations. The company is currently investigating a breach of its operating system.

The incident occurred on Friday, according to the company. Peninsula Energy, which is listed in Australia, requested a trading halt to prepare an announcement regarding the event.

A filing dated Monday described the situation as preliminary while the investigation continues.

title: Tower Records cyberattack potentially leaks 11 million customer records
text:
Japanese retailer Tower Records announced a cyberattack on 19 November 2026 potentially compromised 11 million customer records, including names, dates of birth and delivery addresses.

Tower Records stated that approximately 11 million customer records may have been compromised in a cyberattack that occurred on 19 November 2026. The company confirmed that the leaked data includes personal details such as names, dates of birth and delivery addresses.

According to the company, no credit card information was leaked in the incident. The breach was reported by Japanese news outlets.

title: SOCRadar: AI agent used to target European banks
text:
SOCRadar research identifies a French-speaking cybercriminal using a jailbroken AI agent to target European financial and municipal sectors.

SOCRadar Research Team has revealed the activities of 'BabidiGhost', a French-speaking operator who targeted European banks, insurers, payment providers, and municipalities in November 2026.

The operator spent nine days using a jailbroken AI agent to execute the campaign. According to the report, the operator issued commands in plain, misspelled French, delegating the technical execution to the AI agent.

title: KEPCO confirms breach exposing 1.5 million individuals
text:
South Korea's main power utility confirmed a breach of its billing and procurement systems, exposing sensitive data for over 1.5 million individuals.

Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) confirmed on 20 November 2026 that a threat actor accessed its internal network, specifically targeting the KEPCO ON electricity billing platform and the electronic procurement system (SRM). The company stated it detected the unauthorised access on that date and subsequently blocked external IP addresses and suspended the affected services to contain the incident.

According to KEPCO, the breach exposed personal and financial details for 650,487 customers, including names, ID information, bank account numbers, and card details. Additionally, data for 426,827 company representatives and 442,934 employees was compromised, with the latter group's exposure including employee ID numbers and contact information. The company attributed the breach to "advanced technologies such as AI" but provided no specific details on the initial access vector or attack chain.

A threat actor using the alias "Noiem" claimed responsibility on a hacker forum on 19 November, advertising the theft of user data, supplier records, and bidding documents. While South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission confirmed KEPCO received a theft claim email on that date, attribution to Noiem remains unconfirmed. KEPCO is notifying affected individuals and coordinating with government and financial authorities to m

title: Riken suspends Fugaku supercomputer after external intrusion
text:
Japan’s Riken institute has cut off external access to the Fugaku supercomputer after detecting suspicious traffic that allowed an outside party to tamper with internal servers.

Riken suspended operations of the Fugaku supercomputer and severed external access after detecting suspicious traffic on its user authentication system. In a notice dated 17 November, the institute stated that an outside party used a public dashboard displaying Fugaku’s operational status to breach the system’s internal operations network.

The intrusion resulted in the tampering of multiple servers. Riken said that the names, email addresses, and user IDs of up to 4,597 Fugaku and RIKYU users may have been exposed.

title: NSA restores normal operations after PHP patching caused internal network outages
text:
The US National Security Agency has returned to normal operations after patches to PHP caused disruptions to its internal classified communications network, NSANet, for three days.

The National Security Agency (NSA) confirmed it is now operating under normal conditions following three days of disruptions to NSANet, the internal network used for classified communications. The outages were attributed to maintenance affecting PHP, a commonly used programming language. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated that patching following the maintenance caused some systems to fail to restart as expected.

While the agency has resumed business as usual, certain facilities remain under “Code Orange” for non-essential employees, requiring delayed openings and supervisor check-ins. A Friday morning voicemail indicated the agency was operating under “normal conditions, with exceptions.”

Administration officials insisted the incidents were not the result of a cyberattack and were not connected to recent IT issues affecting Microsoft products, airline travel, or online banking. Sources familiar with the situation reported that intelligence operations at NSA Georgia, focused on the Middle East, were not negatively impacted, and the outages did not curtail support for President Donald Trump’s trip to Asia.

title: House report warns US firms on Chinese open-weight AI risks
text:
A joint congressional report urges US companies to stop embedding Chinese open-weight AI models, citing national security risks and the difficulty of removing such dependencies.

A 50-page joint investigative report from the House Homeland Security Committee and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party warns that US companies are increasingly embedding China-developed open-weight AI models into their tech stacks. The report identifies Airbnb, DoorDash, and Anysphere (owner of the Cursor coding platform) as examples of firms using these models for customer assistance, coding, and inventory management. None of the firms immediately responded to a request for comment.

The report draws on hearings, classified briefings, and agency advisories, stating that the investigation uncovered risks that "American businesses, policymakers, and national security officials can no longer afford to overlook or downplay." It compares the situation to the rapid adoption of Huawei and ZTE technology, warning that removing Chinese open-weight models from US infrastructure could take several years and cost taxpayers billions.

According to the report, federal investigators found that Chinese developers used proxy networks and fraudulent accounts to harvest outputs from American frontier models to replicate their capabilities. The report includes 12 policy recommendations, such as building an American open-weight AI initiative, creating an AI bill of materials, and barring China-developed

title: Kirsten Davies appointed US National Cyber Director
text:
The Department of War CIO replaces Sean Cairncross as the new National Cyber Director.

Kirsten Davies, currently serving as Chief Information Officer at the Department of War, has been appointed as the new National Cyber Director. She replaces Sean Cairncross, who was confirmed for the position in August 2025. Davies previously held senior security roles at Unilever, The Estée Lauder Companies Inc., Hewlett-Packard, Siemens, and Barclays.

The appointment follows a series of significant outages across the US, including disruptions to Microsoft 365, the Federal Aviation Administration, and JPMorgan Chase. The Trump Administration has stated there is “no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor behind the recent tech outages.”

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Secretary of State Marco Rubio explained that the incidents were unrelated and stemmed from companies patching vulnerabilities and upgrading outdated systems. This context coincides with a reported surge in AI-assisted cyberattacks, primarily powered by the Chinese agentic AI penetration testing framework Artex.

title: FBI investigating apparent hack of National Crime Information Center
text:
The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the NCIC, a critical database used by law enforcement agencies nationwide, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a person familiar with the matter told the Associated Press. The NCIC is a computerised database of criminal justice information available to local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, containing records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history, and stolen property.

The bureau declined to comment on the incident, which was first reported by CNN. The scope of the problem was not immediately clear. President Donald Trump, speaking in a Fox News Channel interview, said: “We just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good.”

The incident comes as the US government has experienced a series of digital outages, which administration officials have attributed to routine system upgrades rather than cyberattacks. There was no immediate indication that the FBI incident was related to those outages. The bureau has historically been a frequent target for hackers, including a September incident where the group ShinyHunters claimed to have obtained data on FBI employees and compromised the bureau’s jobs portal.

title: CISA warns of active exploitation of SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway flaws
text:
CISA warned that threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in the wild: one in SAP NetWeaver and one in Cisco Expressway devices.

The US cybersecurity agency CISA warned on Friday that threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in the wild: CVE-2025-42884 in SAP NetWeaver and CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway. The alert follows a warning from Russian cybercrime prevention firm F6, which stated that attacks began shortly after proof-of-concept code for the Expressway flaw was released publicly.

CVE-2025-42884 is a medium-severity issue (CVSS 6.5) in SAP NetWeaver that allows unauthenticated attackers to leak or modify server information by injecting JNDI environment properties. SAP patched this bug in its November 2025 security updates. CISA noted there appear to have been no reports of exploitation before its Friday alert.

CVE-2026-76466 is a critical hardcoded credentials weakness (CVSS 9.8) in Cisco Expressway Core and Edge devices configured in a cluster. The flaw allows attackers with persistent cookies to connect to the database service and execute system commands with root privileges. Cisco patched the defect on 21 October in Expressway Series release X15.5.20. CISA added the Expressway flaw to its KEV catalogue on 20 November, urging federal agencies to patch within three days.

title: GL.iNet patches remote management flaw exploited to deploy malware
text:
A threat actor exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud platform to install malware on routers and KVM devices, prompting the vendor to recommend installing a security firmware update.

China-based networking hardware maker GL.iNet has warned that a threat actor exploited a vulnerability in its cloud-based remote management service, GoodCloud, to deliver malware to some routers and KVM devices. The vendor discovered the flaw on 20 November and has since patched it, but stated that the fix does not remove existing malware from infected devices.

GL.iNet recommends that customers install a separate "security firmware" on all devices, even those showing no signs of infection, to ensure malware is removed. It remains unclear who is behind the attack or how many devices were compromised. Additionally, it is unknown whether attackers reached the computers connected to the compromised KVM devices.

RemoteToHome Consulting, which manages a large number of GL.iNet routers, reported that most of the nearly 200 routers it checked appeared to be impacted, either by this new attack or an older backdoor dating back to September 2025. Based on its code analysis, RemoteToHome said the attack worked because the GoodCloud software ran commands from cloud messages without checking them, a claim GL.iNet has not confirmed.

title: PHP patches phpAfterShell flaw enabling RCE via session corruption
text:
PHP has released patches for CVE-2026-126714, a critical vulnerability that allows remote code execution by exploiting interrupted session writes to trigger object deserialization.

Security firm Depthfirst identified a critical-severity vulnerability in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-126714 with a CVSS score of 9.2. The flaw, dubbed phpAfterShell, exists because PHP overwrites session files without emptying them first. If a session write operation is interrupted mid-process, the file retains mixed content: fresh session data followed by remnants of the old session. This corruption can cause ordinary strings to be interpreted as serialized object data, leading to remote code execution when the session is subsequently loaded.

According to Depthfirst, attackers can trigger this by controlling data written to a session file and interrupting the write operation, for example through multipart upload progress updates. The issue is related to the earlier PHP2Shell flaws, where PHP’s upload-progress callback could open and decode a file-backed session before the target script began. Although PHP added restrictions on object creation in memory, it did not modify the underlying file update behaviour, leaving the attack path viable.

title: N-able patches critical SSRF flaw in Mail Assure
text:
N-able has released a patch for a critical server-side request forgery vulnerability discovered during its investigation into a cyberattack on its Mail Assure and SpamExperts services.

N-able disclosed that it has remediated a critical server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, which was identified during its investigation into a cyberattack targeting its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services. The company confirmed that the attack involved a web server where attackers likely accessed stored credentials, leading to the temporary suspension of services including logging, mailbox synchronisation, and the management portal on 16 November.

The vulnerability, which carries a CVSS score of 9.3, exists because the affected service did not restrict the destination of the LDAP synchronisation connection check performed when a relay is configured. This flaw could allow an API user with sufficient privileges to force the vulnerable server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, identify reachable services, and send crafted data to internal systems.

N-able stated that it has contained the incident, changed credentials, and revoked API and OAuth tokens. Access to the Mail Assure and SpamExperts dashboard and APIs was restored on 21 November. The company reported that exploitation was confined to a single N-able-hosted server and that continued monitoring has found no further malicious activity. A formal root cause analysis is expe

title: Norwegian energy firms hit by Azure API Management flaw
text:
Norway's NSM confirmed that Equinor and Skagerak Energi were targeted via a security issue in Azure API Management, which Microsoft has now patched.

Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) stated that an unidentified threat actor exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft Azure API Management (APIM) to target access tokens and sensitive credentials. The agency said the issue affected organisations across multiple sectors in Norway and abroad, though it remains unclear how extensively the flaw has been exploited.

Equinor, which operates the Mongstad refinery, said it detected the attack on Tuesday but did not fully contain it until Friday. The company reported that oil and gas production continued normally and there is no indication that data was stolen or altered. Skagerak Energi, a majority-owned subsidiary of Statkraft, disclosed a separate incident on Wednesday, stating that operations were unaffected and no information compromise was found.

Microsoft told Recorded Future News it identified and fixed a security flaw affecting the Developer, Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers of Azure API Management, as well as the older 'Classic' tiers. The company said it discovered the issue on 18 November and closed the access path the following day. Microsoft warned that hackers may have accessed passwords and other sensitive information stored in vulnerable systems before the fix was deployed, particularly where customers had not used Azure Key Vault for secure storage.

title: Azure APIM flaw exploited to target Norwegian energy firms
text:
Microsoft closed an access path in Azure API Management that allowed unauthorised access to secrets, impacting Equinor and Skagerak Energi.

Microsoft identified a security issue in Azure API Management (APIM) on 18 November and closed the access path the following day. The vulnerability allowed threat actors to access secrets stored in APIM Classic instances, including named values, client secrets for identity providers, subscription keys, and tokens for direct management APIs. Microsoft stated that APIM Classic tiers not following documented security guidance were affected, while v2 tiers were not impacted.

Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) confirmed on 20 November that the vulnerability affected several organisations, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi. Equinor reported the attack on 17 November, stating it found no evidence that data was stolen or altered. Skagerak Energi disclosed the incident on 18 November, noting no impact on operations or production and no evidence of information compromise. NSM said an unknown threat actor targeted tokens, secrets, and named values, with impact extending to several sectors in Norway and abroad.

Security expert Anders Kristiansen warned that credentials lifted from APIM could be used against outside services, with the extent of exposure depending on each credential’s permissions. NSM advised APIM users to treat their secrets and named values as compromised and replace them.

title: Azure API Management flaw exploited to steal API credentials
text:
Microsoft confirmed a vulnerability in Azure API Management Classic tiers was exploited to access stored secrets, with Norwegian authorities linking the incident to attacks on energy companies.

Microsoft issued a security advisory stating that an unauthorized party could have used a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers to access stored secrets. The company identified the issue on 18 November 2026 and deployed a mitigation on 19 November 2026, which closed the unauthorized management-plane access path. However, Microsoft warned that this remediation does not automatically invalidate credentials that may have been accessed prior to the fix.

Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) linked the vulnerability to cyberattacks against energy companies, including Equinor and Skagerak Energi. NSM stated that an unknown threat actor targeted access tokens, secrets, and named values stored in Azure API Management. Equinor disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on 17 November 2026 but later reported that the attack had stopped and no data was stolen or altered. Skagerak Energi reported an attempted attack with no operational impact or evidence of compromised information.

Microsoft specified that the vulnerability affects APIM Classic tiers, while APIM v2 tiers are not impacted. The exposed data may include secrets in Named Values, client secrets for identity and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys, and tokens for direct management APIs. NSM advised organisatio

title: Cisco Expressway RCE added to CISA KEV
text:
Cisco has released a fix for a critical remote code execution flaw in Expressway Series devices that CISA has listed as known exploited.

Cisco issued a security advisory on 21 October 2026 for CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series. The flaw, rated 9.8 on the CVSS v3.1 scale, allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root. The vulnerability stems from the use of persistent cookies and insufficient validation of client certificates when TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering.

According to the advisory, an attacker with possession of the cookies can connect to the database service and invoke specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands to achieve this. Cisco confirmed that the vulnerability affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices, both virtual and appliance versions, if they are running a vulnerable release and are configured in a cluster.

In November 2026, the vulnerability was added to the Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) database of the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). Cisco stated it does not have direct evidence of active exploitation but strongly recommends upgrading to a fixed software release, as no workarounds are available.

title: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack disrupted services
text:
The EU executive body confirmed an AI-assisted attack in late October disrupted key systems, though no staff data breach was found.

The European Commission has confirmed it was the target of an AI-assisted cyberattack detected on 22 October and confirmed on 26 October. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier stated that the attack has been largely contained, with no evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff. As a protective measure, several applications were temporarily taken down, most of which have since been restored.

According to Politico, the incident caused disruptions lasting over 10 days and potentially compromised large amounts of data. Impacted services included the Commission’s HR platform Sysper, the medical reimbursement system MyPMO, and translation systems. Regnier did not attribute the incident to a known group and said he was not aware of any ransom demand.

The disclosure follows a warning from CERT-EU regarding threat actors using the AI-powered penetration-testing framework Artex. CERT-EU assessed that Artex’s public availability would likely accelerate adoption by threat actors, resulting in more frequent, faster, and more scalable automated attacks. Artex has previously been used in attacks against Barracuda, Railway, and ConnectWise customers.

title: Careers360 breach exposes 22M records including exam results
text:
A dataset of 22 million records from the Indian education platform Careers360 appeared on a public forum, containing sensitive academic and personal data.

In November 2026, data allegedly taken from the Indian education and careers platform Careers360 appeared on a public hacking forum. According to Have I Been Pwned, the dataset comprises 22 million records, including 3.6 million unique email addresses.

The compromised data includes names, phone numbers, genders, and caste categories. Most records also contain students' entrance exam results, specifically ranks and marks. The breach was added to the Have I Been Pwned database on 20 November 2026, with attribution to 'Threat Actor 888'.

No specific vendor advisory or confirmed exploitation status beyond the data's appearance on the forum is provided in the source.

title: Too Lost breach exposes 724k unique email addresses
text:
An unauthorised party claims to have obtained data from music distributor Too Lost, exposing sensitive personal and financial details for 724k unique email addresses.

In November 2026, an unauthorised party claimed to have obtained data from Too Lost, a music distributor for independent artists. According to Have I Been Pwned, the compromised dataset contains 724k unique email addresses belonging to artists, their collaborators and fans.

The data reportedly includes bcrypt password hashes, partial credit card data (last 4 digits and card type), and identity verification information (in some cases, passport, driver's licence or national ID numbers). Additional fields include dates of birth, physical addresses, IP addresses, and payment histories.

Too Lost stated that its investigation remains ongoing and that external forensic specialists have been engaged. The company said measures have been taken to secure affected systems and credentials, and it is working with advisors to coordinate communications and support for affected individuals.

title: Container Store restores systems after cyberattack
text:
Neighborhood Intelligence confirmed The Container Store has restored its website and systems following a weekend incident that disrupted online ordering and in-store transactions.

Neighborhood Intelligence, the parent company of The Container Store, stated that the retailer has restored its website and systems following a cybersecurity incident that occurred over the weekend. The disruption forced the company to shut down online ordering systems and implement alternative transaction-processing procedures in its approximately 100 US stores, although physical locations remained open.

The company said it engaged cybersecurity experts to contain the incident and restore affected systems. While it reported that the incident did not affect other brands under the Neighborhood Intelligence umbrella, such as Bed Bath & Beyond or Overstock, it did not address claims made by the cybercriminal group n0n, which listed the company on its leak site earlier this month.

According to cybersecurity firm LevelBlue, the n0n group has primarily targeted healthcare and pharmaceuticals but recently claimed to have data from financial services and retail firms. LevelBlue noted that the group uses AI coding agents and paid AI services to write and debug attack scripts, helping it scale operations quickly.

title: Indian juvenile held for selling Agniveer data on dark web
text:
A 14-year-old was detained after allegedly extracting personal data from 4,000 former Agniveers via an unauthorised access to a government registration portal.

Indian investigators have detained a 14-year-old for allegedly gaining unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register for employment opportunities in other government departments. According to the report, the juvenile allegedly extracted personal information from the site and posted an advertisement on the dark web claiming to possess the data of approximately 4,000 individuals.

title: Illinois officials probe apparent cyberattack on Algonquin Dam
text:
State authorities are investigating an apparent cyberattack on the Algonquin Dam in McHenry County.

Illinois state officials are investigating an "apparent cyberattack" on the Algonquin Dam, located on the Fox River in McHenry County, according to a report by Todd Feurer.

The Illinois Department of Natural Resources stated that the incident occurred on Monday. Staff immediately took action to prevent any unauthorised access and to ensure the dam continued to operate.

State officials did not provide further details.

title: Bromcom breach exposes 355k UK school email addresses
text:
A data breach at UK education software provider Bromcom exposed 355k email addresses and SSO reference numbers, though the company states no passwords or system access were compromised.

In September 2026, UK education software provider Bromcom suffered a data breach involving a legacy single sign-on (SSO) registration system. The incident exposed 355k unique email addresses belonging to staff and pupils at UK schools, alongside SSO registration reference numbers.

Bromcom confirmed that no passwords or authentication tokens were exposed. The company stated that the incident did not enable access to Microsoft or Google accounts or its school management system. The breach was added to the Have I Been Pwned database on 23 November 2026.

title: CISA flags Cisco Expressway RCE flaw as actively exploited
text:
CISA has added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, warning that attackers are using the flaw to gain root access on Internet-exposed Cisco Expressway devices.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) ordered federal agencies to patch a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Cisco Expressway Series devices within three days. Tracked as CVE-2026-76466, the flaw stems from hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster.

Cisco released security patches in late October, stating that its Product Security Incident Response Team was not aware of active exploitation or public proof-of-concept exploits at that time. However, CISA tagged the vulnerability as actively exploited on Friday and added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday. The agency urged all network defenders, including private-sector teams, to prioritise patching to block ongoing attacks.

Russian cybersecurity company F6 reported that attackers used an unnamed AI assistant to exploit the vulnerability on Internet-exposed devices. According to F6, the attackers compromised two Internet-facing devices, used one to access two additional internal cluster nodes, and then deployed custom Python scripts to scan for SMB resources, interact with SQL

title: Critical NGINX flaws enable unauthenticated remote code execution
text:
NGINX has released fixes for five critical vulnerabilities, including use-after-free and integer underflow bugs, that allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code.

NGINX announced on 18 November 2026 that it has fixed multiple critical vulnerabilities affecting releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8. The flaws, identified as CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, and CVE-2026-123634, permit remote unauthenticated attackers to crash worker processes or execute arbitrary code. Cisco’s PSIRT confirmed that proof-of-concept exploit code is available, though it is not aware of any malicious use to date.

The vulnerabilities include a use-after-free in the mail proxy module and HTTP/2 proxy handling, as well as an integer underflow in HTTP/2 flow control. According to Palo Alto Networks, these issues specifically impact configurations where HTTP/2 is enabled. The vendor noted that the flaws allow attackers to trigger heap-based buffer overflows or prematurely free memory for active connections, leading to remote code execution.

Major vendors including Fortinet, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks have published advisories detailing the impact on their respective product lines. While Fortinet is still investigating the impact on its portfolio, Cisco has identified several affected products, including Identity Services Engine and NX-OS Software, with fixed releases scheduled for December 2026. Palo Alto Networks has confirmed that PAN-OS versions prior to

title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
text:
Broadcom has released emergency patches for a critical authentication bypass in VMware vCenter Server, which Mandiant says was exploited in zero-day attacks by a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group since September 2026.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server. According to Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to bypass authentication and gain administrative control over the server, thereby compromising the virtual machines it manages. Broadcom released the fix on 19 November 2026 in advisory VMSA-2026-0009, classifying it as an emergency update with no official workarounds, though network restrictions and firewall controls may reduce exposure.

Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) documented that a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group, tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221), exploited the flaw in early September 2026. The researchers said the attacks were part of a broader intrusion campaign where the group first compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances before moving laterally to target VMware infrastructure. The attackers used a custom Golang tool named BONESAW to exploit the vulnerability, creating an administrator session and stealing the directory database.

Following initial access, the threat actor deployed tools such as SAWSNAKE to perform Golden SAML attacks, forging authentication tokens to bypass multifactor authentication and impe

title: Bell Canada confirms 'agentic' actor stole enterprise data
text:
Bell Canada confirmed that an 'agentic' threat actor breached its Maximo system on 17 November 2026, exfiltrating enterprise customer details including IP addresses and contact information.

Bell Canada has confirmed that an "agentic" threat actor accessed its systems on 17 November 2026, stealing enterprise customer data. The breach involved unauthorised access to a pre-production environment of the company's Maximo system, which is used to order and provision telecommunications network connections.

According to a breach notification reviewed by BleepingComputer, the data may have included business contact details such as names, job titles, corporate email addresses, and phone numbers. The dataset may also have contained ticket titles, some IP addresses associated with network elements, and limited contextual information. Bell stated that the affected data did not include credentials, highly sensitive personal information, or file attachments.

Bell said it contained the incident immediately and that there has been no impact to customer services. The company is sharing indicators of compromise (IOCs) and threat-hunting information with enterprise customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS), though it has not publicly released these indicators. Bell has not identified the threat actor or disclosed the number of affected customers.

title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to expose tenant metadata
text:
Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft Entra Connect Health to steal administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data, prompting Microsoft to deploy a server-side fix.

Microsoft has warned organisations that a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service was exploited to gain unauthorised access to tenant-level metadata. The company discovered the flaw in the Entra Connect Health API on 9 November 2026, after it was first introduced on 23 July. An investigation concluded on 20 November 2026 that unauthorised read-only access had occurred, though no unauthorised configuration changes were identified.

The exposed information included email addresses for tenant technical contacts and administrator accounts, tenant IDs, display names, and regional information. It also covered Microsoft Entra license tiers, directory synchronisation status, and an expired certificate previously used to register Connect Health agents. Microsoft stated that user passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, and on-premises server topology details were not exposed.

Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on 19 November 2026 to prevent further exploitation and began notifying affected organisations. The company has not disclosed the number of impacted tenants or the identity of the threat actors.
